📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal are eyeing Stuttgart central defender Finn Jeltsch ahead of the January transfer window, according to reports in Germany.

Jeltsch made his first-team debut for Stuttgart back in February 2025 having joined the club from German second-tier outfit Nurnberg earlier that winter.

The 20-year-old has gone on to establish himself as one of the brightest young talents in Bundesliga football, making 62 appearances in all competitions across his two-and-a-half year spell in Stuttgart.

Towards the end of last season, Jeltsch got his hands on his first piece of silverware at club level as Stuttgart got the better of Arminia Bielefel to win the German Cup for the first time in 28 years.

There was another career highlight for Jeltsch just last week as he made his senior international debut as a second-half substitute in Germany’s thumping 5-0 victory over the Netherlands in the Nations League.

According to Bild, Jeltsch’s outstanding form has not gone unnoticed overseas and a number of clubs have had Jeltsch on their radar for ‘quite some time’, including Arsenal.

It’s claimed the reigning Premier League champions are ‘closely monitoring’ Jeltsch’s progress from afar and will continue to check on the centre-half over the coming weeks and months.

Liverpool are also being credited with a strong interest in a hotly contested race which will only become more competitive if Jeltsch continues on the same meteoric trajectory.

The report adds that Stuttgart are yet to receive any concrete offers for Jeltsch, who has a market value of around €35million (£29m).

Jeltsch, who is also comfortable playing as a defensive midfielder, has three-and-a-half years remaining on his current contract with Stuttgart.

‘So far, it’s been a steep climb,’ Stuttgart head coach Sebastian Hoeness recently noted of Jeltsch’s rapid development.

Sources indicate that ‘He came here in 2025 and immediately established himself as a regular starter, playing at a very high level. That is difficult to ignore, of course.

‘He brings a very high level of skill. On top of that, he’s a fantastic guy.

‘He wants to develop, be professional, and pursue his goals with all his might.’.

Industry observers note that hoeness added: ‘It will be very exciting to see where his path leads. There are no limits.’.

‘With speculation swirling over Jeltsch’s future, Hoeness encouraged the centre-back to block out the noise and try to concentrate on the here and now.

‘It would be good for him not to look too far into the future and to focus on his own development,’ he added.

According to recent reports, ‘He will do that, I’m not worried about it at all. He has everything it takes.’.

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith.

VAR was correct not to overrule Michael Oliver after he awarded a controversial penalty against Morgan Rogers for handball against Leeds, per Dermot Gallagher.

The match was level at 1-1 when Rogers attempted to block a shot from Jayden Bogle. He turned his back in doing so and the ball appeared to catch him on his upper arm, with Oliver immediately pointing to the spot.

Sources indicate that VAR reviewed the incident and allowed the penalty to stand, which Dominic Calvert-Lewin duly buried to put Leeds 2-1 up. The match ended 4-1 in the visitors’ favour.

Chelsea fans were left confused by the decision, with many suspecting the ball had caught Rogers above his sleeve and thus did not warrant handball. Rogers, meanwhile, appeared to protest that the ball had hit him in the face.

Xabi Alonso was similarly unimpressed with the decision, saying post-match: “I don’t agree. I think that it was harsh from Michael Oliver. For me it was not a penalty.”.

But, speaking on Sky Sports’ Ref Watch, former Premier League referee Gallagher has opined that VAR was correct to allow Oliver’s decision to stand, pointing out that there was not sufficient evidence to overturn it.

The VAR reviewed a number of different angles of the incident, but none conclusively absolved Rogers.

“You can watch replays, you can watch a multitude of angles, some will say it hit (Rogers) on the elbow and some say the face,” remarked Gallagher. “There is no conclusive evidence to say the referee is wrong, so he has to give a penalty.

“We are not trying to prove the referee wrong. He gave a penalty. What I am saying is there is no evidence to say the referee is wrong, not that the VAR is gonna say ‘this is the right decision’.

“The referee has given the decision, and the evidence says the referee is not wrong.”.

Jay Bothroyd concurred, admitting he felt that the ball might have hit Rogers too high, but that he would not have liked to see the penalty overturned.

Industry observers note that “You have got to stick with the referee's decision,” he declared. “It looked like it hit his sleeve but they have a camera to show the elbow. It is difficult to see.

“When you look at that, (everyone has) an opinion), so you have to stick with the referee's decision.

Breaking: KILMARNOCK 2 ABERDEEN 4: Dazzling Dons get a Frick pick-up but it's more misery for McCann's men

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (971 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:33 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:15 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Having been bored senseless by the football offered up under Stephen Robinson, Aberdeen supporters were – at the very least – crying out for the next appointment to provide some sort of entertainment to get excited about over the dark winter months.
  • It has been revealed that in Mario Frick, they may have got their man.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 15:33 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:15 EST, 21 November 2026.

Having been bored senseless by the football offered up under Stephen Robinson, Aberdeen supporters were – at the very least – crying out for the next appointment to provide some sort of entertainment to get excited about over the dark winter months.

It has been revealed that in Mario Frick, they may have got their man. Whether or not the former Luzern boss will be a success at Pittodrie is anyone’s guess. But on this evidence, it’s going to be a lot of fun watching him have a go.

At times, they were scintillating here on their way to a thrilling win which moved them five clear of their hosts and provided some much-needed breathing room ahead of a tricky upcoming schedule which involves trips to Ibrox and Tynecastle, as well as two home clashes against the Dundee clubs.

Sources indicate that yes, it wasn’t perfect. Far from it, in fact. Defensively, they were far too open. Kilmarnock just weren’t good enough to take full advantage.

But you suspect that will be forgiven to an extent as long as they can play with this level of panache and aggression going forward.

Findlay Marshall celebrates after scoring the Dons' fourth goal at Rugby Park.

Sources indicate that frick has arrived with the promise of bringing ‘heavy metal’ football to Pittodrie. It’s taken a little over 90 minutes to understand what he's talking about.

Sources indicate that ‘It was very chaotic,’ he admitted. ‘It's quite different to Switzerland, because there is technicality, but it’s not as physical as it was today.

Sources indicate that ‘It was difficult. We were lucky as well because Killie, especially in the second half, played very well, but I think at the end it's a deserved victory.

‘When the players were young, they didn’t think about mistakes, didn’t think about any negatives.

‘They played only to win for fun, and I told them to play as if they were young players and I think, especially first half, it was very good.

‘You don't know what's going on or what can happen in this first game, so I'm very happy we won.’.

Frick shows his delight after tasting victory in his first match in charge of Aberdeen.

Kilmarnock spurned a golden opportunity to take a sixth-minute lead at the end of a rapid counter-attack, with Joe Hugill finding himself all alone in the Dons box.

The striker took a heavy first touch, allowing Marius Muller to quickly narrow the angle and block the effort. It’s easy to see why Hugill has found the back of the net just twice this year.

And the hosts were made to pay for that miss within 90 seconds as Aberdeen went in front.

Sources indicate that for the umpteenth time this season, Killie failed to clear their lines under little pressure, with Stuart Armstrong teeing up Kevin Nisbet to sweep home a lovely finish from the edge of the area. The unsighted Nico Mantl in the Killie goal didn’t even move.

Mind you, he should have done significantly better four minutes later as Nisbet notched his second of the afternoon.

The keeper’s positioning as the Dons striker stepped up to send a low free-kick in off the post was as poor as it gets.

You got the feeling that the walls would have caved in had Aberdeen grabbed a third, but a brief drop-off in intensity from Frick’s side enabled Killie to drag themselves back into the contest.

A bit of pinball outside the Dons box saw the ball fall favourably for skipper Greg Kiltie 12 yards out, who adjusted his body brilliantly to drill beyond Muller on the half-volley.

Yet with a defence as dodgy as this, manager Neil McCann can never feel overly confident.

Ante Palaversa – terrific on his first appearance of the season – was given far too much time in the centre circle to get his head up and pick out Nesta Guinness-Walker on the left.

He glided past MJ Kamson-Kamara as if he wasn’t there before dinking a ball right on to the head of Brad Lyons, who rose completely unopposed to power home against his former employers.

If Killie continue to defend like this, relegation is a certainty. Will the manager even get the chance to turn it around? Going off the abuse being hurled in his direction from the home punters, his jacket is evidently on a shoogly peg. Many fans have already made up their mind.

Nisbet's free-kick finds the net for his second as the Dons take control of the game.

Sources indicate that michael Schjonning-Larsen’s deflected effort from 20 yards shortly after the restart looked destined for the goal before Muller instinctively leapt to his right to claw it away on the line. It was a superb stop.

His next contribution defied belief.

Goodness knows what the keeper was thinking as he tried to pass out from the six-yard line, playing it straight to the feet of Tyreece John-Jules – only just on the park – who steadied himself before finishing.

You would have stuck your house on Nisbet putting this one to bed with five minutes remaining, however with just Mantl to beat, he pulled his left-footed effort wide.

Findlay Marshall showed him how it’s done with stoppage-time looming, running half the length of the field before drilling low into the corner to consign Killie to another sobering defeat.

McCann said: ‘I probably sound like a broken record, but we create really major, big chances, and we don't take them.

It has been revealed that ‘We're letting games pass us by. We're giving teams the opportunity to start ahead of us because of the goals we're conceding and then it's difficult to work back.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Roy Keane has predicted the biggest threat to Arsenal’s hopes of retaining the Premier League title is unlikely to come from any of their traditional rivals.

The Gunners displayed unfamiliar signs of vulnerability at St James’ Park on Saturday evening where they let a half-time lead slip, before eventually battling back to earn a 2-2 draw.

The loss of two points was compounded by an injury to goalkeeper David Raya who is now nervously anticipating the results of a forthcoming MRI scan on his damaged arm.

Manchester City’s failure to win at home against Fulham meant the failure to cling onto the lead Arsenal gained through Eberechi Eze’s first-half opener represented a missed opportunity.

With Enzo Maresca’s side in the midst of a disappointing run and the likes of Chelsea and Liverpool struggling to come to terms with the demands of their newly introduced managers, Arsenal are widely expected to defend the title they won back in May.

Indeed, their nearest challengers at present are Brighton, who are thriving under the management of Fabian Hurzeler, and Keane sees no reason why the Seagulls can’t continue to mount a challenge.

‘At this moment, yes,’ Keane told Sky Sports when asked if Brighton could emerge as the only team capable of preventing Arsenal from claiming back-to-back titles.

‘That’s because of the form they’re in, they’re goal threat and defensively they’re very, very good.

‘They’ve got a top quality manager but obviously over the next couple of months the pressure and injuries and whatever (will come).

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Industry observers note that ‘They’ve got a young team and have a lack of experience. But at this moment in time they’ve got to enjoy it and keep that pressure on Arsenal.’.

Hurzeler, who masterminded a 3-0 win over the Gunners back in September, has plenty of admirers and was recently linked with the Manchester United job.

‘His time will come,’ Keane said when it was put to him that the German would’ve represented a better appointment than Mauricio Pochettino.

It has been revealed that ‘We talk about Poch getting close a few times and sliding doors moments. He’s done a great job and Brighton and if he left now you’d be looking at him and thinking he should’ve stuck at it a bit more.

‘We talk about loyalty in football and it’s got to work both ways. So I’m glad he continuing at Brighton and hopefully they can continue having a good season.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri.

It has been revealed that I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

David Raya was not involved in Arsenal’s open training session on Monday morning.

The Spaniard was forced off in the second half of Arsenal’s 2-2 draw with Newcastle in the Premier League on Saturday evening, as the Gunners dropped two points at St James’ Park.

Raya suffered what looked like a shoulder injury during a seemingly innocuous collision with Newcastle striker William Osula.

He went down hurt and required treatment, and had to be replaced by deputy Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Raya appeared to be in significant pain as he came off and Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta admitted after the match that it was “not good news”.

Raya was sent for scans on Sunday and while the results of those have not yet been confirmed by the club, he did not train with his team-mates on Monday morning.

Kepa and Illan Meslier went through the usual goalkeeping drills without their team-mate at London Colney.

It leaves Raya as a major doubt for Arsenal’s Champions League match at home to Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night.

Arteta will provide an update on Raya’s injury and any potential spell on the sidelines at his pre-match press conference later on Monday.

The big matches come thick and fast for the Gunners in the coming weeks.

Arsenal host Manchester City in the Premier League at the weekend, before making the short trip across north London to take on arch-rivals Tottenham seven days later.

There are also showdowns with both Real Madrid and Manchester United coming up before Christmas.

By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 09:13.

European football returns to the Emirates Stadium on Tuesday evening, when Arsenal welcome a Borussia Dortmund side just one point below them in the Champions League rankings.

The Gunners have navigated their opening four matches unbeaten to collect 10 points and sit third in the table, while Niko Kovac's side have lost one and won three in the continent's top tier so far to lie 12th.

Here, Sports Mole runs through everything you need to know about how to tune into the contest.

It has been revealed that arsenal vs. Borussia Dortmund is scheduled for an 8pm kickoff on Tuesday, November 24.

In a recent development, another six matches will commence at the same time, including Manchester City vs. Napoli and Real Madrid vs. PSV Eindhoven.

Arsenal are hosting Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium, where Mikel Arteta's men have won each of their first six games in all tournaments this season, conceding just two goals in the process.

BVB last visited Arsenal's home turf in 2014, when Yaya Sanogo and Alexis Sanchez propelled the Gunners to a 2-0 group-stage victory.

According to recent reports, arsenal vs. Borussia Dortmund will not be shown on terrestrial television in the UK; instead, the fixture will be broadcast on Amazon Prime Video.

Fans with an Amazon Prime Video subscription can watch the game on a variety of devices, such as via the TV app, phones, computers and games consoles.

Amazon Prime Video costs £8.99 a month for the full Amazon Prime package, or £7.99 a month for just Amazon Prime Video, although the latter is only available to select accounts.

Highlights of the match will be made available on the Amazon Prime and TNT Sports YouTube channels shortly after full time, as well as the official Arsenal account.

The @primevideosport X account will also post short clips of key moments as and when they happen.

In a recent development, top spot in the Champions League table is within Arsenal's reach, as the third-placed Gunners are just two points behind Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain, the latter of whom do not take to the field until Wednesday vs. Roma.

Arteta's men will therefore rise to first for at least 24 hours if they win and Real Madrid lose to PSV, or if they triumph, Los Blancos draw and Arsenal also make up a -1 goal difference to Jose Mourinho's side.

The Gunners could also equal two Champions League records, as they are a win or draw away from matching their longest-ever run of unbeaten group stage/league phase games (17) and could also draw level with Liverpool's English record of 13 consecutive group stage/league phase wins at home.

On the other hand, Dortmund are capable of rising into the top eight automatic qualification places with a shock win in North London, but head coach Kovac has only won one of his previous five Champions League matches against an English club; a 7-2 thrashing of Tottenham Hotspur with Bayern Munich in 2019.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The chaotic saga of litigation which followed the 2025 AFCON final will finally be resolved this week, as the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) prepares to release its final decision.

The champion of AFCON 2025 remains in dispute after the scandalous events of January 18th, where Senegal were stripped of a 1-0 victory after their squad briefly left the pitch in the second half.

Recent findings suggest that an unprecedented and unsavoury series of events followed. Morocco appealed the result and won, before Senegal escalated the affair to CAS in Lausanne, the world’s premier body for the resolution of sporting disputes.

Now, ten months after the full-time whistle was blown in Rabat, AFCON 2025 will finally have an undisputed champion, though the animosity will surely remain, regardless of the verdict.

Here is everything you need to know about the situation ahead of the final verdict being released...

An official press release from CAS confirms the decision will be released on Tuesday, November 24, 2026.

It has been revealed that no specific time of day has been set. The press release simply says the decision will be released “in the course of the afternoon.”.

Morocco and Senegal met in the AFCON 2025 final, but the match was beset by unprecedented controversy.

Late in regular time, Morocco were awarded a penalty, which Senegal protested by leaving the pitch.

Industry observers note that players and staff, led by head coach Pape Thiaw, alike returned to the changing rooms, and the match was paused for 14 minutes. Some Senegal players remained on the pitch and returned to the pitch only at the behest of captain Sadio Mane.

Crucially, the referee never abandoned the match, and play resumed once the entire Senegal squad had returned to the pitch.

Brahim Diaz then missed the vital penalty and Senegal went on to win in extra time, with Villarreal’s Pape Gueye scoring the decider.

In March 2026, two months after the final, CAF announced the shock decision to reverse the result, saying Senegal had forfeited the match by leaving the pitch.

The result was thus changed to a 3-0 win for Morocco, who are now considered the AFCON 2025 champions.

The Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) immediately hit back at CAF’s decision to strip them of the AFCON title, and have since refused to return the trophy, which they have regularly paraded in public.

The FSF immediately appealed CAF’s decision and the case fell to CAS. CAF president Patrice Motsepe acknowledged Senegal’s “right” to do so and added that he will “respect the decision that’s taken at the highest level.”.

The government of Senegal has also criticised CAF’s move, expressing “profound dismay” and questioning the governing body’s credibility.

The Moroccan football federation, meanwhile, has called for tournament rules to be “respected” as they maintain their status as champions.

Gary Neville was left ‘absolutely stunned’ by Mauricio Pochettino’s decision to recall Matthijs de Ligt after the defender’s blunder allowed Liverpool to make their breakthrough in a rampant 4-0 victory over Manchester United.

A seemingly innocuous hoiked pass over the top from Liverpool full-back Ronald Araujo wreaked havoc inside United’s half in the tenth minute, leading to Dominik Szoboszlai’s superb opener.

De Ligt had been thrown in for his first appearance of the Premier League season and there were obvious signs of rustiness early on as the Dutchman bizarrely let Araujo’s hopeful ball run through to Alexander Isak.

Isak’s eyes will have lit up as he raced in behind in acres of space and United were guilty of yet more calamitous defending just moments later as Leny Yoro clattered into the back of the Liverpool striker on the edge of the penalty area.

Referee Samuel Barrott wasted little time in showing Yoro a straight red card for the clumsy foul, reducing the visitors to ten men in a nightmare start to Pochettino’s reign as manager.

United’s woes were soon compounded as Szoboszlai struck the resulting free-kick emphatically beyond a despairing Senne Lammes to break the deadlock and send the Anfield crowd into raptures.

Liverpool were not done there, though, and it was Florian Wirtz who directed home Rio Ngumoha’s cross with an audacious flicked finish to double the hosts’ advantage inside only 13 minutes.

A pair of well-taken goals from Ngumoha and Victor Munoz further increased the deficit in a dominant second half for Andoni Iraola’s men, who finished the weekend three points clear of Bournemouth in fourth place.

When watching back replays of the catalogue of errors leading to Liverpool’s opener, former United full-back Neville revealed just how ‘stunned’ he had been left by the decision to select De Ligt in the first place.

It has been revealed that ‘That is just a basic ball over the top of him. It’s his problem to start with.’.

Though De Ligt was the main focus of Neville’s criticism, Yoro did not escape without receiving some barbs of his own.

‘Leny Yoro can be further across but if you look at De Ligt in this channel, he’s miles away from him,’ Neville added.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Yoro should be across, yes, he can get further around. He has to cover and he doesn’t. He reacts late, his anticipation is really poor.

‘And because he doesn’t play the ball, Yoro, it could be outside the box but it is a red card.

‘It’s so clumsy from Yoro, he makes a lot of these kinds of mistakes.’.

According to Neville, Yoro had displayed great ‘naivety’ in getting himself sent off so early in the Premier League contest.

‘He’s not happy with it, Mauricio Pochettino,’ the ex-England international continued.

‘You could argue with it, Isak just delays slightly to make sure that Yoro runs into the back of him.

‘But unfortunately, when you’re a young defender, you’re going to get caught like that and it’s naivety.’.

Switching his focus back to De Ligt, Neville said the Netherlands international had likely been ‘exposed’ as a result of playing so little football over the last 12 months.

According to recent reports, ‘We saw it against Como and he’s been out for a year, trying to come back to this level of football. It’s really tough,’ he went on.

‘To have De Ligt out there in a game like this, in a back four, he’s been exposed inside the first ten minutes.

It has been revealed that ‘I have to say, Yoro’s positioning covering is really poor. It’s poor.

‘Yoro has got to be across and around the other centre-back. You’ve got to cover your mate and he doesn’t. It’s really just bad all round from Manchester United.

‘Michael Carrick will be watching this at home and thinking, “Yeah, that’s what I was having to deal with two weeks ago”, it’s so poor.’.

Neville’s Sky Sports’ colleague Jamie Carragher was similarly unimpressed by United’s defending, branding the visitors’ start ‘absolutely shocking’.

‘It’s as bad as it gets from two centre-backs,’ the former Liverpool and England defender said.

‘The ball from Ronald Araujo… it wasn’t even a pass, it’s just a clearance, a hopeful ball through the middle.

Roberto De Zerbi accused former club Marseille of using him as a "scapegoat" despite him giving "everything" for them.

De Zerbi took charge of Marseille in June 2024 on a three-year contract and led them to a second-place finish in Ligue 1 in his debut campaign.

He also came within seconds of winning the Trophee des Champions in the following campaign, but Goncalo Ramos scored a 95th-minute equaliser for Paris Saint-Germain to take the game to penalties, and Marseille lost the shootout.

De Zerbi's tenure did not last much longer after that; a Champions League league-phase exit was followed by a 5-0 Classique hammering, which resulted in his departure in February.

The Italian was not out of a job for long, signing with Tottenham at the end of March, but he has now hit out at Marseille for what he feels was unjust treatment.

"Many times, I was the scapegoat for everyone, but in such an crucial club and city, everyone has to take responsibility, not just a few people, of whom I was one," De Zerbi told Canal+, as quoted by TNT Sports.

"I'm sorry, because when I signed for Marseille, I wanted it so badly and I thought I would stay for many years.

"However, some people didn't keep their word to me. They told me things they didn't follow through on. A year and a half had passed before the Champions Trophy in Kuwait.

In a recent development, "We were on the verge of winning a title after a 12-year drought. Since that match, the situation deteriorated; it worsened until my departure.

Sources indicate that "Marseille is one of the clubs I hold closest to my heart, along with Foggia. I suffered a lot when I left. I suffered because I gave everything in Marseille.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino said Manchester United were on the wrong end of an ‘unfair’ decision during their heavy Premier League defeat to Liverpool.

Pochettino’s reign as United manager began in dismal fashion at Anfield as his side were thumped 4-0 by arch-rivals Liverpool.

The defining moment of the match came after just eight minutes as Leny Yoro was sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak as he raced through on goal.

Isak’s touch was heavy and United goalkeeper Senne Lammens swiftly retrieved the ball but referee Samuel Barrott still deemed a red card to be the suitable punishment.

To make matters worse for Manchester United, Dominik Szoboszlai blasted home the subsequent free-kick to put the hosts ahead.

Liverpool scored again just five minutes later – Florian Wirtz volleying home a cross from the lively Rio Ngumoha.

England winger Ngumoha, 18, scored Liverpool’s third 20 minutes into the second half before Víctor Munoz added a fourth late on.

Pochettino described his first match as Manchester United manager as ‘painful and disappointing’ but criticised the early red card that paved the way for the heavy defeat.

Sources indicate that ‘So painful. So disappointed,’ Pochettino mentioned in his post-match interview. ‘It’s not ok to start a game in the Premier League with this situation.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Recent findings suggest that ‘The game changed completely after six minutes. Now we can explain everything but the damage is done, it’s so painful.

Recent findings suggest that ‘The players are so, so feeling the pain of the result. I told them to the calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality.

Leny Yoro is SENT OFF after eight minutes! 😱 pic.twitter.com/VKYvckvBBP.

According to recent reports, ‘We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field. We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.’.

Pochettino, who was hired as Michael Carrick’s replacement last week, added: ‘The ball was for the goalkeeper. In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak.

‘When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper; he runs and goes down.

‘In Leny’s case, it wasn’t intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal, everyone who plays football can feel it.

According to recent reports, ‘If you look before, on the sixth minute. Jacquet on Mbeumo. Similar? No. If you compare the actions, that was a penalty.

It has been revealed that ‘How that changes life, if you score after six minutes. Now, for sure, we are talking in a different way. We have to take responsibility; I take the responsibility. We keep pushing.

It has been revealed that ‘It’s not going to change what happened. Being respectful is the most notable. At the same time, I have to defend my club. And tell what I feel.

‘That was an action that everyone who plays football, it was clear that a situation that was not a red card.’.

Manchester United dropped into the relegation zone prior to the November international break, when Carrick was relieved of his duties.

Results over the weekend leave the Red Devils second from bottom in the Premier League with just eight points from their first 11 games of the campaign.

Liverpool, meanwhile, climb back into the Champions League places after an emphatic win over United.

Anfield boss Andoni Iraola said: ‘We have been very good away this season but at home we haven’t been good enough and still haven’t been good enough.

‘We needed a big game, and Manchester United is always a big game, to finish like this.

‘It’s true the game’s condition changes because they play with 10 most of the game, but still we’ve done our job, we controlled the game and I think it’s always nice when you can win like this in these kind of games.’.

Recent findings suggest that asked for his take on the early red card, Iraola added: ‘I think he’s the last man, no? It’s a clear foul and a red card, yes?’.

Industry observers note that man City vs. Napoli will be shown live on TNT Sports 1 or TNT Sports Ultimate for viewers in the UK.

You can also view this match on the TNT Sports YouTube channel and both clubs' official YouTube accounts.

At the halfway stage in the League Phase, Man City sit seventh in the 36-team standings after accumulating nine points from their opening four matches.

Enzo Maresca’s side will realistically need at least a couple more victories to ensure they finish inside the top eight and secure automatic qualification for the last 16, rather than slip into the playoffs.

The Citizens have won each of their last three Champions League meetings with Napoli, most recently winning 2-0 on home soil in the League Phase of last season’s competition courtesy of goals from Erling Haaland and Jeremy Doku.

Napoli will therefore be out for revenge when they make the trip back to the blue side of Manchester, while Wednesday’s fixture also marks the return of City legend Kevin De Bruyne, whose first comeback to the Etihad was cut short.

Indeed, he was the unfortunate one sacrificed after just 21 minutes following a red card for Giovanni Di Lorenzo in Napoli's 2-0 defeat last season.

The Italian club have won one and lost three of their opening four UCL games this term, suffering a disappointing 4-1 defeat at Porto on November 4, and currently sit down in 27th place in the table, six points behind the top eight.

While Napoli enter this contest on the back of a narrow 1-0 home win over Torino in Serie A on Saturday, courtesy of a Scott McTominay goal, Man City were held to a frustrating 1-1 draw by Fulham in the Premier League.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino has already admitted that newly introduced employers Manchester United are in a relegation battle - with some key trends and statistics highlighting why the Red Devils should be genuinely worried about the drop.

Man Utd offered little resistance on Pochettino’s managerial debut at Anfield on Sunday as they were ripped apart 4-0 by arch-rivals Liverpool following the early dismissal of Leny Yoro.

Fans will have seen that during their own season of constant struggle last term, Tottenham already had 18 points on the board at this stage of the campaign - 10 more than United’s current tally.

Spurs only confirmed their Premier League survival on the final day, edging out rivals West Ham by a single point in a hugely dramatic finish.

There are more alarming numbers and patterns from Premier League history that do not bode well for free-falling United’s fortunes this season.

Over the past 20 years, at least one team in the bottom three after 11 games has gone on to be relegated by the end of the season.

In total, 56.66 per cent of clubs in the relegation zone after 11 matches have finished there.

Pochettino’s side will take solace in the fact that seven teams have previously beaten the drop after picking up exactly eight points from their opening 11 fixtures.

In a recent development, but that doesn’t tell the full story. Teams with only eight points and sitting in the relegation zone after 11 games have survived on just two previous occasions, with six dropping down to the Championship.

Only Newcastle in 2006/07 and Southampton in 2019/20 beat the drop after starting off with eight points from their first 11 games to languish in the bottom three.

Ipswich sat outside the relegation zone in 2023/24 with eight points from 11 matches, but were unable to stay up come May.

Over the last 20 years, 31 teams with eight points or fewer from their opening 11 fixtures failed to survive; only 24 sides stayed up with that starting tally.

In more concern for United, the other two teams right now in the relegation zone make up six of those latter examples.

Crystal Palace are used to starting slow - twice they have begun the season with four points from 11 games, only to record 11th-place finishes on both occasions.

In total, the Eagles have recovered from eight points or fewer after 11 games to stave off relegation four times, while Sunderland have achieved that feat twice.

What does United’s own history tell us about the current side’s chances of beating the drop?

When United were last relegated from the top-flight, all the way back in 1973/74, the Red Devils had a higher points total after 11 games.

Under the current rules for three points for a win, rather than the two awarded at that time, Tommy Docherty’s side would have had 11 points from their first 11 matches of the 1973/74 First Division season.

In a recent development, in reality they had just nine, after three wins and two draws. Goalkeeper Alex Stepney was their joint-top goalscorer after converting two penalties.

United finished the season 21st out of 22 teams, five points from safety. Perhaps United fans will take solace from the fact that this season’s start more closely resembles the beginning of the campaign prior to that relegation - five draws, one win and six losses from 12 games.

In 1972/73, United managed to salvage an 18th-place finish in the old First Division, comfortably beating the drop. Of course, the next season they were relegated for the first time since 1938.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have notified the Football Association (FA) that they intend to appeal Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool.

The Red Devils were reduced to 10 men just eight minutes into Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Man Utd boss at Anfield on Sunday.

Liverpool then romped to an easy 4-0 win, with Pochettino afterwards lamenting referee Sam Barrott’s decision to dismiss Yoro as “unfair”.

The Argentine believed that his player did not deny a goalscoring opportunity, meaning that he should not have seen red.

Yoro clipped the heels of Alexander Isak as the Liverpool attacker bore down on goal, but Pochettino and United fans felt that goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have reached the loose ball before Isak, negating the goalscoring potential.

Under current FA rules, clubs have 14 days to submit an appeal, with United back in action on Saturday as they host Brentford in the Premier League at Old Trafford.

With his current three-game domestic suspension, Yoro would also miss the trip to Newcastle and visit of Coventry early next month, but remain available for Champions League meetings with Sporting and RB Leipzig.

Yoro’s dismissal on Merseyside was his second in two months, having also received his marching orders in a Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid in October.

Former United boss Michael Carrick questioned that decision at the time and stated his belief that it was not a red card, but no appeal was made by the club.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Florian Wirtz was quick to shut down any suggestion that Liverpool were spending too much time ‘thinking about’ Arsenal after their 4-0 win over Manchester United.

Mauricio Pochettino’s reign got off to a nightmare start in what was ultimately a mismatch between the two bitter rivals, with the Red Devils proving their own worst enemy and giving themselves a mountain to climb early on at Anfield.

Some calamitous defending from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro led to Dominik Szoboszlai’s tenth-minute breakthrough and saw the latter shown a straight red card by referee Samuel Barrott, a decision that only compounded the visitors’ woes.

The impressive Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s advantage with an audacious finish just three minutes later to send the home crowd into raptures, before a pair of second-half goals from Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz completed the rout.

Having cut a frustrated figure on the touchline for the most part, Pochettino made it clear he was less than impressed by the officiating on show as he faced the media shortly after the final whistle on Merseyside.

The Argentinian will no doubt be desperate to turn the tide when United return to Premier League action at home to Brentford in six days’ time, following a midweek trip to Sporting.

The result ensured Pochettino’s men finished the weekend just one point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace, with the Old Trafford giants now leading Europe’s top five leagues for most goals conceded (34 in all competitions).

Liverpool, meanwhile, moved four points clear of fifth-placed Bournemouth and just one point behind Arsenal’s two nearest rivals, Manchester City and Brighton, after ten games.

‘Really good. The atmosphere after the game was so good. We could enjoy it and it was just a nice afternoon,’ Wirtz – named man of the match – remarked of the victory in his post-match interview with Sky Sports.

‘I feel very good but it’s also because the team develops and gets better.

‘Just being part of this, you also get better, so I’m just enjoying that.’.

Asked if he was perhaps benefitting from being coached by Andoni Iraola and Jurgen Klopp at club and international level, Wirtz replied: ‘Both are very good coaches and I enjoy playing under both.

‘They both bring different qualities and I’m just happy and can be happy to have two of these coaches.’.

Victory in next Sunday’s Merseyside derby at Everton would see Liverpool move to within four points of Arsenal, who host Manchester City later that same afternoon.

When asked if the 4-0 thumping of United had taken Liverpool to ‘another level’, Wirtz replied: ‘Yeah, it was definitely crucial today, also for the table situation.

‘I think a lot of teams on top of the table, they didn’t win this weekend so it’s good that we could use the chance.

‘The red card influenced the game a bit of course but we take that, we earned it because of the run of Alex [Isak] so yeah, very good.’.

Wirtz was then asked if he was ‘thinking about’ Arsenal and possibility of winning the league this season, and his answer was unequivocal.

It came after the Gunners – the reigning Premier League champions – surrendered a first-half lead to drop points away to Newcastle.

‘Uh, I wasn’t talking about Arsenal… all the teams, I don’t know, from one to three,’ Wirtz responded.

‘So we knew, we didn’t speak so much about it, but I think everybody knew it was a big chance to make some points.

‘I’m happy we used this chance.’.

By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 09:36.

Arsenal loanee Ethan Nwaneri will reunite with his parent club when Borussia Dortmund take on the Premier League champions in Tuesday's Champions League clash at the Emirates Stadium.

The 19-year-old joined the German giants on a season-long loan during the final hours of the summer transfer window, but he is yet to find his best form under Niko Kovac.

Nwaneri has only provided one assist and no goals from his first 13 appearances in a Dortmund shirt across all competitions, that contribution coming on his Bundesliga debut against Hoffenheim.

Since then, the 2007-born playmaker has only started four Bundesliga matches, and he is still waiting to make a first XI in the Champions League, being restricted to 87 minutes across four substitute outings.

Nwaneri was also given just a one-minute run-out in the weekend's 1-0 Bundesliga win over Borussia Monchengladbach, but he may be given the chance to strut his stuff against his boyhood team.

Recent findings suggest that champions League rules permit loan players to face their parent clubs in the Champions League, so Nwaneri will be able to feature in Arsenal vs. Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night.

Unlike in the Premier League and other domestic competitions in England, where loan players cannot take on parent teams without special dispensation, there are no such restrictions outlined in the Champions League rules and regulations.

However, if Nwaneri was to return to Arsenal in January, the England Under-21 international would not be able to feature for the Premier League champions for the remainder of the tournament.

Article 30.05 of UEFA's Champions League regulations states that 'A player may not play in the UEFA Champions League, UEFA Europa League or UEFA Conference League for more than one club in a single season', but Arsenal are not expected to bring Nwaneri back to North London over the winter.

The teenager has scored 10 goals and set up two more in 51 Arsenal games since making his debut against Brentford in September 2022, when he became the Premier League's youngest player of all time.

Loan players making decisive contributions against parent clubs in the Champions League has been a semi-regular occurrence, the most notable example being Philippe Coutinho in 2020.

The then-Barcelona playmaker was shipped out to Bayern Munich and reunited with La Blaugrana in the quarter-finals of the 2019-20 edition, when he incredibly scored twice in an 8-2 annihilation.

Sixteen years prior, Fernando Morientes - on loan at Monaco from Real Madrid - scored in both legs of the quarter-final against Los Blancos, helping Les Monegasques knock out his parent team on away goals before they lost to Porto in the final.

Recent findings suggest that real were also stung by James Rodriguez in the 2017-18 semi-finals vs. Bayern Munich, but the Colombian's goal - which he refused to celebrate - was not enough to prevent Los Blancos advancing 4-3 on aggregate.

The 2013-14 semi-finals saw Thibaut Courtois play a crucial role in Atletico Madrid's success against parent club Chelsea, who tried to force Los Rojiblancos to pay them £2.5m for each game the Belgian goalkeeper played against them, only for UEFA to rule the terms null, void and unenforceable.

As for Blackburn, they responded to Tony Mowbray stepping down from his first-team duties with a 2-2 draw at rivals Burnley on Sunday.

Having twice come from behind, Rovers will be satisfied with a deserved share of the spoils at Turf Moor, a result that keeps them 11 points above the relegation zone despite being viewed as one of the favourites for the drop in the summer.

Furthermore, 17 points have been accumulated from their last 10 games, emphasising that they could still challenge for a top-eight spot this campaign.

However, Blackburn remain with just one away win this campaign, only recording seven points from eight matches while shipping 15 goals.

Peter Schmeichel believes simply avoiding relegation should be Mauricio Pochettino’s main ‘target’ at Manchester United this season.

Pochettino took charge of United for the first time away to bitter rivals Liverpool on Sunday afternoon and it proved a nightmare start for the Argentine, with his side thumped 4-0 at Anfield.

The Red Devils were reduced to ten men in only the tenth minute after Leny Yoro brought down Alexander Isak, and the visitors’ woes were compounded as Dominik Szoboszlai scored with the resulting free-kick.

Man-of-the-match Florian Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s advantage with an audacious finish just three minutes later, before a pair of second-half goals from Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz put the hosts out of sight.

The result ensured United remained firmly in the relegation zone at the end of the weekend’s drama, only one point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace.

The Old Trafford giants, who now lead Europe’s top five leagues for most goals conceded (34 in all competitions), will look to stop the rot when they switch their focus to Champions League matters at Sporting on Wednesday evening.

Three days later, Pochettino’s men return to Premier League action at home to Brentford.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Realistically, can Manchester United just finish tenth or 12th? It would be okay,’ former United goalkeeper Schmeichel said on Viaplay following the side’s heavy defeat on Merseyside.

‘I know it’s silly to say but we are in the relegation zone and this team looks like a team that could get relegated.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘So now that should be the target. Weirdly enough, at the moment it looks like it [that avoiding relegation is the target].

‘But we [Viaplay’s punditry panel] have all played in the Premier League so we know we’re in November, we’re approaching December, it’s not really now.

‘It’s when we get to March and if they keep doing this for so long, I mean there’s going to be trouble.

‘But I think, at least I have faith that he [Pochettino] can correct those things.

‘He’s never going to make them a championship winning team, not these guys.’.

It was some calamitous defending from Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro that led to Liverpool’s breakthrough against United, with the latter guilty of fouling Alexander Isak after failing to cover his centre-back partner.

And while it was De Ligt that made the initial mistake, Yoro was the main focus of Schmeichel’s post-match criticism.

‘I think Isak is doing really well,’ the Dane noted when watching back replays of the move.

‘When Yoro comes in, Isak cuts across him and yes, he brings him down.

Industry observers note that ‘It’s terrible defending, it is. Not for that on its own but why is he not reading the ball over the top, over De Ligt?

‘Yoro should have been supporting his co-defender and he’s not.’.

Schmeichel has long been an outspoken critic of Lisandro Martinez and branded the defender ‘disgraceful’ in the wake of United’s 2-0 loss to Chelsea last month.

It came just a fortnight after Martinez had introduced an explosive attack on United’s board, in which he suggested the squad had been repeatedly let down by the club’s recruitment team.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I’m fed up talking about him. Honestly, I’m fed up talking about him,’ Schmeichel said of Martinez following United’s latest setback.

‘He’s a guy that criticises people upstairs, criticises his team-mates… I think you have to perform better than that, I really do think that.

‘You can through not all of the goals, but you can go through a couple of the goals and he’s there, at the centre of that, and he could have done something to at least make it harder for Liverpool to score.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino has already instituted a major change at Manchester United in a bid to lift the club’s standards and dodge relegation.

The Argentine’s United tenure got off to a grim start at Anfield on Sunday as Leny Yoro was shown an early red card and Liverpool went on to bag four goals.

The result leaves the club 19th in the Premier League, with the prospect of relegation - or, at the very least, being involved in the relegation battle - more real than ever.

But as Pochettino discovers the true scale of the task at hand, he has wasted little time in imposing his methods on United.

That has begun with scrapping a rule imposed by his predecessor Michael Carrick, who was sacked during the November international break.

While in the job, Carrick had habitually handed the United squad a day off following a match, but Pochettino has promptly done away with that provision.

His players reported to Carrington bright and early on Monday morning for recovery sessions, with a Champions League meeting with Sporting looming on Wednesday evening.

Pochettino has pushed forward their arrival time, too, with some players touching down at the training ground as early as 8.30am.

It has been a busy few days at Carrington. Pochettino has hired a upcoming strength and conditioning coach to help accommodate his focus on high-pressing football, while the club are also appealing Yoro’s red card.

They are doing so on the basis that Senne Lammens looked set to beat Alexander Isak in his footrace, and, thus, Yoro’s clumsy tackle did not constitute denial of a goalscoring opportunity.

"The ball was for the goalkeeper. In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak.

“When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper, he runs and goes down.

MOTHERWELL 1 RANGERS 2: Naderi rides to the rescue as wasteful Ibrox men get out of jail with late winner

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 18:01 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 18:10 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • FOR a team that just couldn’t find a way to get the ball into the net, no matter how they tried, it was always going to take a couple of jammy deflections or something out of the ordinary to get out of jail.
  • It has been revealed that and that’s exactly how it panned out with just two minutes left on the clock.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:01 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 18:10 EST, 21 November 2026.

FOR a team that just couldn’t find a way to get the ball into the net, no matter how they tried, it was always going to take a couple of jammy deflections or something out of the ordinary to get out of jail.

It has been revealed that and that’s exactly how it panned out with just two minutes left on the clock. Rangers, tied at 1-1 and in danger of falling six points behind arch-rivals Celtic at the head of the Premiership, were throwing everything bar the kitchen sink at their hosts.

Balls were being blazed high and wide of the target. Chances were being passed up left, right and centre. It looked like Derek McInnes’ men were destined to rack up a third straight away draw in the league and take the club’s record to three years without a win at Fir Park when, in the 85th minute, substitute Findlay Curtis saw an effort parried by Alex Paulsen, Dujon Sterling blasted the rebound towards goal and Motherwell’s No 1 somehow flung an arm in the air and diverted it onto the crossbar.

According to recent reports, it looked like the last throw of the dice. Until Ryan Naderi, who had suffered a miserable evening up to that point, made the difference.

A speculative shot from Badredine Bouanani from the edge of the area whacked off the outstretched boot of Martin Moormann and fell into the Czech internationalist’s path on the right.

His jabbed effort towards goal was nothing to write home about, but it carried just enough juice on it to whack off the hapless Moormann again, change direction and fly into the net.

Messy? Yes. Did Naderi care, though? Not a bit. He ran straight into the Rangers crowd behind the goal and lost himself in the relief and jubilation of a victory rescued from the fire.

Recent findings suggest that that’s all that matters right now. Rangers won to keep up the pressure at the head of the table.

Naderi celebrates his late winner that snatched all three points for Rangers.

McInnes applauds the travelling supporters after his side kept pace with Celtic at the top.

However, there is a recurring problem with this squad. This game should have been out of sight, but missing chances and lacking that killer instinct manager McInnes demands remains a serious problem.

Just look at the stats. Rangers had 29 shots on goal in this affair and 11 on target. It should have been a procession, really. In the end, they only got through by the skin of their teeth.

There are times when these players look like they couldn’t hit a cow on the backside with a banjo and that is going to trip them up substantial-time in this title race unless they sort it out tout-suite.

They started like a runaway train in this game and got off to the perfect start with Manny Fernandez heading home from a corner within the first 10 minutes.

The problems started when Naderi, just nowhere as convincing in the role of main striker as he is when played with the likes of Kevin Kelsy, benched last night before a late cameo, up beside him, started missing sitters.

Industry observers note that jake Girdwood-Reich then levelled for Motherwell with pretty much their first forage upfield and it all got way more uncomfortable than it should have been. It is something McInnes is going to have to sort out.

The match started exactly the way McInnes would have wanted following the return from the international break with Rangers in the ascendancy from the first whistle and a goal to the good after eight minutes.

It was also as straightforward and as simple a goal as you could wish to see. One from a set-piece which Motherwell really ought to look back upon with some serious self-reflection. It was just too easy.

Industry observers note that djeidi Gassama had won a corner on the left thanks to a cross being deflected wide by Tom Sparrow. Kim Minsu fired in the flag-kick and Fernandez rose unchallenged to nod the ball home from close range. Like taking candy off a baby.

Fernandez gets his head to Minsu's corner to put Rangers in front early on at Fir Park.

Fernandez milked the celebrations in front of the home fans after netting his first goal of the season, but Minsu’s reaction was tinged with the same senses of jubilation and relief.

The South Korean had been getting himself in a twist over failing to deliver an assist so far in his Rangers career. Now he’s off the mark on that front, it’s time for him to satisfy the demands from McInnes for a goal as well.

Shortly after the opener, Naderi, leading the line in front of Minsu, with Kelsy having been left on the bench, should have made it two.

According to recent reports, an initial chance fell to the Czech internationalist after a Gassama shot had broken to him in the area. Moormann, however, put in a fine tackle to deflect the ball wide for a corner-kick.

Minsu took charge of that situation and fed it to Gassama, whose shot from a central position was parried by Paulsen.

It fell perfectly for Naderi and he should have buried a close-range header that ended up being cleared by Moormann again.

Fail to take your chances when on top and the prospect of getting yourself into bother is always there — and that’s what happened to Rangers on 21 minutes.

Motherwell had barely been up the park. Barely been in the game. However, they won a corner on the right thanks to some decent forward play from Regan Charles-Cook, on for the injured Ibrahim Mentioned, and made the very most of the set-piece.

Emmanuel Longelo played a short corner to Sparrow who fired a low ball into the area at pace.

Girdwood-Reich timed his diagonal run nicely to move into space in front of a static Olwethu Makhanya and his first-time effort with the right foot beat visiting goalkeeper Ivor Pandur to his right to settle in the bottom corner.

Girdwood-Reich turns home Sparrow's cross to equalise for the home side.

Nico Raskin had a shot touched over by Paulsen just before the half-hour and, moments later, it took a good saving tackle from Fernandez at the other end to deny Seb Palmer-Houlden a shot at goal after he had surged into the area.

With Motherwell getting their tails up before the interval, a ragged-looking Rangers really needed something to get a grip back on the game. It came just before the break with a one-on-one chance squandered by Naderi.

He had done well to get himself into a position where he could see the whites of Paulsen’s eyes, but the home keeper came out on top in the end by getting down low and touching the striker’s angled shot wide for a corner.

After Dan Neil had sent a low sidefooted effort just wide from the edge of the area and Palmer-Houlden had forced a save from Pandur with an unconvincing effort, Rangers passed up a super opportunity a little before the hour mark.

Naderi did well to set up Minsu in an unmarked position on the left side of the area. That elusive first goal in Rangers colours — or, rather, the foul red-and-black mish-mash that is their ‘third kit’ — beckoned.

Sources indicate that unfortunately, Minsu’s effort was awful. A straight-up sclaff that indicated a player just trying too hard or actually beginning to let a lack of confidence or a touch of anxiety interfere with his technique.

Whatever the reality, his poorly hit shot was saved at the near post by Paulsen.

Rangers did come close when a Tuur Rommens cross was deflected by Sparrow onto his own near post and Gassama then blazed a terrible effort over from a promising position.

When Paulsen made that double save, it looked like Motherwell had done enough to get a valuable point until Naderi got the visitors over the line by hook or by crook near the death.

It has been revealed that it shouldn’t take this much effort and pain for Rangers to win a game of football, though. They need to show they can be cold-eyed killers if they want to win this title.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Villarreal have rubbished a bizarre online rumour claiming Nicolas Pepe required eye surgery after he filmed himself taking in the solar eclipse.

Reports circulating on social media over the weekend suggested Pepe had sustained damage to his retina during the lunar event back in August, which had supposedly forced the forward to miss five matches.

A resurfaced video, which Pepe himself had uploaded to Snapchat, demonstrated the 31-year-old winger observing the eclipse in Spain without the use of protective glasses.

According to recent reports, ‘To all the idiots on my Snapchat, that is a solar eclipse! In France, all they got was a little croissant from the bakery,’ Pepe joked at the time.

Unsurprisingly, the wild rumour swiftly spread online amongst fans, many of whom mocked Pepe for apparently going against the advice of experts and wilfully exposing himself to intense visible light, ultraviolet and infrared radiation.

But on Sunday evening, Pepe’s club Villarreal released a statement vehemently denying these baseless claims on social media.

‘Villarreal CF, in response to reports published in various media outlets recently, clarifies that it is completely false that Nicolas Pepe’s eye surgery has any connection to observing the solar eclipse,’ the statement from the La Liga outfit read.

Villarreal confirmed that Pepe had indeed undergone surgery but stressed that it was ‘entirely unrelated’ to the solar eclipse.

‘The surgery had been scheduled in advance for reasons entirely unrelated to this event,’ the statement continued.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘The club urges accuracy and responsibility when reporting on matters related to its players’ health.’.

The surgery Pepe underwent meant the ex-Arsenal attacker was sidelined for Villarreal’s games against Real Madrid, Napoli, Elche, Liverpool and Valencia last month.

The Ivory Coast international made his return in Villarreal’s Copa del Rey first-round tie with Manacor, in which he scored his side’s final goal in a thumping 5-0 victory.

He has gone on to feature in all of Villarreal’s next four matches, although he has failed to complete 90 minutes in any of those contests.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Since joining Villarreal from Trabzonspor back in 2024, Pepe has made a total of 86 appearances for the Spanish club, chipping in with 14 goals and 18 assists in that time.

Villarreal surrendered an early two-goal lead to lose 3-2 at Barcelona on Sunday and sit tenth in La Liga after 13 matches.

Pepe became Arsenal’s club-record signing when he signed from Lille for a fee of £72million back in 2019 – and the move remains the third most expensive deal in the Gunners’ history, behind those involving Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes.

Despite enjoying an encouraging start, Pepe badly struggled to live up to expectations at the Emirates and has often been branded one of the worst signings of the Premier League era.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher believes a red card for Leny Yoro during Manchester United’s 4-0 defeat by Liverpool was the correct decision - claiming it “would’ve been a surprise” if the defender wasn’t sent off.

Man Utd informed the Football Association (FA) on Monday afternoon of their intention to appeal Yoro’s three-game suspension.

After just eight minutes of Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge of United at Anfield, Yoro found himself scrambling to get back after Matthijs de Ligt allowed Alexander Isak through on goal.

Chasing both man and ball, Yoro clipped Isak on the edge of the area - prompting referee Sam Barrott to show a straight red card. At the time Pochettino was spotted aggressively waving his finger, clearly disagreeing with the decision.

But on Sky Sports’ Ref Watch panel, Gallagher couldn’t see any mitigating factors for Yoro.

He said: “If you look at it from the referee's angle, is it a foul? That's the first step. Yeah. Is he in possession of the ball? From that angle, yes.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.
  • In a recent development, this two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic.
  • The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

In a recent development, this two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman mentioned. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

Recent findings suggest that “We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”.

Recent findings suggest that avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

Industry observers note that it had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an issue for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

In a recent development, it did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

Sources indicate that greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

According to recent reports, england thought they had taken the lead in style when goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti gave the ball away needlessly. The excellent Kathryn Batte has run the rule over potential alternatives to Lucy Bronze.

The 35-year-old right-back is out injured, but Ella Toone was called up in her place, rather than a direct replacement.

“Bronze, who is two appearances away from reaching 150 caps for her country, has picked up an injury and returned to Chelsea for treatment,” Batte writes.

“The Lionesses will be missing one of their most reliable players for the matches on Friday and Tuesday, but it gives Sarina Wiegman an opportunity to look at potential replacements for the future.

“Bronze, who has been an integral member of the team throughout Wiegman’s reign, turns 35 later this month. While she will be expected to be the first-choice right-back should England qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, the lack of a recognised back-up has been an ongoing problem.”.

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

“When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman mentioned. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

According to recent reports, “That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

According to recent reports, the Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

Recent findings suggest that all eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”.

According to recent reports, toone quickly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”.

Sources indicate that that opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven major-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.

We will bring you all the build-up, confirmed team news, and live play-by-play coverage throughout the evening.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan put on a show for their fans at San Siro on Sunday evening as they beat Frosinone 5-1 to move back into the top four.

It was a game that promised entertainment from the early stages, and Milan took command thanks to an own-goal from Gabriele Calvani and a much-needed goal from Goncalo Ramos, before Patrizio Masini scored to halve the deficit.

Recent findings suggest that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Sources indicate that the Rossoneri ran away with things in the second half, with Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse netting off the bench before Christian Pulisic got a goal of his own to add some gloss to the scoreline. There were chances to make it an even bigger margin, but five would have to do.

Given that Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus had all won prior to kick-off, it was important that Milan matched their results to keep up the pressure at the top end of the table, and they did so in emphatic fashion.

Ruben Amorim made just one change to the starting line-up from the side that won against Genoa before the break, with Alphadjo Cisse dropping out and Davide Bartesaghi coming in. It was uncertain from the line-up named what the system would be, as has often been the case with the Portuguese coach so far.

Sources indicate that frosinone started the game better and called Mike Maignan into action inside the first minute with a close-range header that was saved, though the flag was up. Then, a deflected strike from Masini on the edge of the box ended up scraping the upright and going behind for a corner.

However, it was Milan who struck first at San Siro. Luka Modric deserves the plaudits for an outstanding through ball to find Adrien Rabiot’s run in behind, and the Frenchman’s square pass was heading towards Christian Pulisic’s run but was turned into his own net by Calvani, leaving Palmisani rooted.

The frantic pace of the early stages continued, as a lovely exchange between Diego Moreira and Pulisic saw a threatening cross turned behind. A few minutes later, Yunus Musah found Moreira who had a shot deflected for a corner, which Goncalo Ramos rose and met well but headed over the bar.

Frosinone kept providing reminders that they too pose a threat going forward, such as on the quarter-hour mark when Kvernadze surged down the left and got off a low shot from a narrow angle that Maignan had to parry behind. The corner wasn’t properly dealt with, and Cittadini flashed one across the six-yard box that Rabiot had to put into the stands.

Just like with the first goal, Milan punished Frosinone for not making the most of their spell of pressure. Goncalo Ramos was the man who started and finished a flowing counter-attack, robbing Calvani of possession before running towards goal. Musah’s through ball was run onto by the electric Moreira, who found Rabiot, and the Frenchman’s cut-back was tucked away by the Portuguese.

Industry observers note that the two-goal lead was very quickly halved though, as Frosinone got the goal their pressure had threatened. Kvernadze’s run down the left and cut-back from the byline was scuffed onwards by Ghedjemis into the path of Masini, who toe-poked it in at the far post.

Recent findings suggest that in the 34th minute, there was a moment that enraged the Milan players, staff and fans. The referee blew his whistle for a shirt pull on Rabiot just as Milan went through on goal with two men in behind and just the goalkeeper to beat. The official apologised, but it felt like a certain goal had been taken away.

It was a half played at a hundred miles an hour, and it ended that way too. Pulisic flashed an effort over the bar from a good position, while Davide Bartesaghi’s low cross towards Ramos was cut out in the nick of time as Milan continued to get joy down the flanks.

It has been revealed that amorim opted to make an intriguing change at half-time, bringing off Bartesaghi and replacing him with Ardon Jashari. This change in turn saw Musah shift to left-back, a role that he played against Genoa in the last match, and from minute one.

Sources indicate that the change proved to be an absolute masterstroke, as Jashari scored inside three minutes. A ball was sent long to Ramos who knocked it down to Rabiot, whose first touch was a lovely through ball to the Swiss midfield. It looked like he had overrun it with the square option not used, but he lashed a shot in at the near post.

According to recent reports, not long after the goal, Ramos gestured towards the bench that he felt some discomfort. He wanted to play through it but Amorim took no risks, opting to bring Alphadjo Cisse on to lead the line.

Industry observers note that there was a rather rare occurrence in the 54th minute, as Milan were awarded an indirect free-kick after Palmisani picked up a back pass from Calvani. Modric laid it off to Rabiot, but the goalkeeper made up for his error with a good save.

In a recent development, continuing the trend of impact substitutions, Cisse got his ninth goal of the season right on the hour mark. A Frosinone corner was cleared and Pulisic found Moreira who had the Italian for company, and he finished the through ball by the Belgian past Palmisani with his trademark composure. The offside flag went up, but after a long check the goal was given.

It has been revealed that milan continued to look like scoring every time they got out of their own half, and Pulisic joined the fun in the 68th minute with a goal of his own. Frosinone again left one man back for a corner that was cleared, allowing the American to easily outpace Terzic with a run from inside his own half, dinking over Palmisani to make it 5-1.

Sources indicate that with 20 minutes left on the clock, Amorim brought Strahinja Pavlovic and Pervis Estupinan on for Diawara and Musah. The final change saw Omari Hutchinson replace Pulisic.

Sources indicate that pavlovic looked far from 100% when he came on, appearing dizzy at certain moments. The head coach seemed to suggest coming off so as not to risk things, but he played on.

According to recent reports, milan had chances to make the scoreline even more impressive, with Moreira and Hutchinson squandering a couple of chances on the break. However, at full-time the team were rightly applauded by the San Siro crowd.
