📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

‘Wake up,’ squawked Gary Neville as he launched into an evisceration of a Manchester United defence that had just capitulated in all too familiar fashion.

The Anfield washing machine, as Mikel Arteta once described Liverpool’s fortress, has accounted for sterner rearguards than the one Mauricio Pochettino has inherited, but there was something particularly abject about this particular 4-0 humbling.

Whether it was the grim acceptance that the eventual scoreline was deemed passable after the most farcical of beginnings to a United managerial tenure, or the immediate removal of any notion that Pochettino has a honeymoon period to enjoy, Neville struggled to compute the reality of the league table as it stands.

‘You play for Man Utd,’ Neville barked, having slapped himself in the face, in surprisingly aggressive fashion, to symbolise the wake-up call his club are in need of.

While he provided an early frontrunner for meme of the season, Neville failed to grasp the full gravity of the situation Pochettino has landed himself in.

Considering the likelihood of United finding themselves in a fully-fledged battle to preserve their Premier League status, Neville was dismissive to the point of arrogance.

‘I don’t believe they’re in a relegation fight,’ he said, without providing a modicum of evidence to explain his confidence.

In a recent development, 🚨| WATCH: Gary Neville has had ENOUGH, slapping himself in the face live on TV after another Manchester United loss. 😳 pic.twitter.com/UovS3bApRk.

‘It’s as bad as it’s been for 55 years but I do think they’ll come out of it and move up the table.’.

Listing the likes of Andrey Santos, unable to nail down a starting slot since his £48million move from Chelsea, Amad Diallo, no Premier League goal in approaching a year, Patrick Dorgu, without a place in the redundant wing-back role he was recruited to fill in Ruben Amorim’s doomed system, and Bryan Mbeumo, immediately sacrificed when United were reduced to 10 men yesterday, as the players best suited to fulfil the requirements of Pochettino’s high-intensity ethos should have prompted an immediate Neville U-turn, even before he threw the name of Bruno Fernandes into the mix, while adding the caveat that ‘he can run around, but whether he knows where he’s running is a bit more debatable’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Make no mistake about it, United are in a dogfight and the situation will only deteriorate further if the dressing room shares Neville’s assertion that this group of players are too good to go down.

Time on the training ground to organise a defence that is now officially the worst in Europe’s top five league is limited and while January will surely bring reinforcements, there is precious little to suggest United have either the funds, or a cohesive enough recruitment strategy to identify the players they require if they are to dig themselves out of trouble.

Sitting second bottom after 11 games is not a small sample size to be dealing with either, especially when you consider the majority of these players were in-part responsible for the multitude of unwanted records that were broken during Amorim’s wretched stint.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that it should also be remembered that Spurs had 18 points after 11 games last season and only stayed up on the final day. United have eight points and have already been beaten by two goals or more on six occasions this term in all competitions.

While Neville’s sparring partner Jamie Carragher may have gotten a little ahead of himself in terms of where Liverpool are at this juncture in Andoni Iraola’s rebuild, he was on the money when assessing how United compare to the teams they should be focused on competing with at present.

‘No-one believes they are, no-one will say that they are (in a relegation fight),’ he stated. ‘But the strength of the Premier League this season, what we could call teams that we expect to be mid-table or near the bottom, I think it’s as strong as it’s ever been.

‘We can talk about teams at the top and say it’s nowhere near as strong. Think about teams in the Champions League. Our teams in this league are not in the top four or five in the Champions League, I don’t think. But when you look at the Europa League or Conference League, we expect our teams to walk it!

‘Look at Fulham, going away to Manchester City, 1-1. Leeds go to Chelsea, 4-1. There are no poor teams. There aren’t many great teams in the league but there are no poor teams. And that’s a problem for Man United.

‘Their next league game is Brentford at home. Manchester United are one of the biggest clubs in the world, Brentford are well-run. If Man United beat Brentford at home, I think we’d all look at that and say ‘great result.’ That will not be an easy game.

He added: ‘The only game they’ve won is Ipswich, a newly-promoted team. In that game they went 1-0 down, Ipswich had another chance. That’s the only game they’ve won.’.

Indeed, United are second bottom, not second top, and until everyone connected with the club accepts that reality and accepts last season’s Michael Carrick-inspired renaissance for what it was, a flash in the pan, the route out of this mess will be a bumpy one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Niko Kovac was under no illusions about the size of the task awaiting his Borussia Dortmund players ahead of facing Arsenal in the Champions League.

Dortmund make the trip to the Emirates Stadium fresh from beating Borussia Monchengladbach on Saturday, a result that moved them two points clear at the Bundesliga summit.

BVB have started a Bundesliga season unbeaten in their first 10 matches for only the third time, after 2002-03 and 2018-19, while their 24 points at this stage is just one fewer than their club record (25 points in 2010-11 and 2013-14).

However, they face an Arsenal side six points clear at the top of the Premier League despite Mikel Arteta's side drawing 2-2 with Newcastle United at the weekend.

The Gunners are also unbeaten in their last 19 Champions League games (W14 D5 – excluding penalty shootout defeats).

Should they avoid defeat here, they will be just the third English team to go 20+ games without losing in the European Cup/Champions League, after Manchester United (25 – September 2007–May 2009) and Manchester City (26 – September 2022–October 2024).

Dortmund also have a miserable record in England, losing eight of their last nine Champions League away games when facing off against sides from the Premier League.

Sources indicate that arsenal have won three of their four Champions League home games against Borussia Dortmund (L1). Their only loss was in October 2013, with Robert Lewandowski scoring a late winner for the visitors in a 2-1 victory.

"We are not only playing against the best defence in England and Europe, but also against the reigning English champions, Champions League finalists last season and the current Premier League leaders," Kovac told reporters.

"We're aware how difficult this is going to be. They have a great team and a great coach. But we're also difficult to play against, and we'll have our chances.".

It has been revealed that home of The Arsenal. https://t.co/qefVsPBSej.

— Borussia Dortmund (@BlackYellow) November 23, 2026.

Kovac has been handed a double injury boost ahead of facing Arsenal, with the Dortmund boss revealing both Serhou Guirassy and Carney Chukwuemeka are available.

Guirassy, who is BVB's top scorer in all competitions with eight goals in 14 appearances, sustained a hamstring strain just before the international break, while Chukwuemeka has recovered from a thigh issue.

In a recent development, "They're ready for tomorrow's match," added the BVB boss. "They're available for selection. We'll have to wait and see whether they'll start or come on as the match progresses.".

Kovac was also asked about the array of English talent that have come through Dortmund's ranks, with the likes of Jude Bellingham and Jadon Sancho enjoying successful spells during their time in Germany.

Frank Lampard and Wayne Bridge for Chelsea in April 2004 (at Highbury) and Harry Kane for Bayern Munich in April 2024 (Emirates Stadium) are the only English players to have scored a Champions League away goal at Arsenal.

Jobe Bellingham and Ethan Nwaneri have both appeared in all four of Dortmund's games in the competition this season, although both are still yet to score.

Nwaneri is cleared to play due to UEFA's rules that allow loan players to play against their parent clubs, with the Arsenal forward yet to register a goal involvement across his 13 appearances in all competitions.

"The Bundesliga is a top league where young talent can come through, especially at Dortmund," Kovac said. "As a club, we are known for developing younger players.

"The English players are very strong physically, technically at the highest level, but the Premier League is the best league in the world and they need playing time.

"A move to Germany, especially Dortmund, is a very good step.".

Mikel Arteta has ruled David Raya out of Tuesday’s Champions League game against Borussia Dortmund but delivered an upbeat bulletin on the goalkeeper’s health.

The Arsenal star sustained an injury during the second half of Saturday’s 2-2 draw against Newcastle.

While it was clear that the Spain international was in significant discomfort, Arteta was unable to clarify the extent Raya’s injury in the immediate aftermath of the game.

The former Brentford shot stopper was reportedly able to drive home once he and his teammates had arrived back from the north east on Saturday evening, but he was absent from Monday’s opening training session.

Asked for an update on the health of his No.1 who underwent MRI scans yesterday, Arteta mentioned: ‘He’s not fit for tomorrow unfortunately but it doesn’t look too serious and we need more tests tomorrow but it’s quite encouraging with the pain that he was showing immediately after the action.

‘We were all quite worried but it seems to be better than what we expected.

‘The doctor explained what happened but it’s quite technical and when you look at the action there doesn’t seem to be much, but the extent of the pain that he had and the pain he had was quite worrying.’.

He added: ‘We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had at that moment. The first test we have done highlights something much more encouraging.

‘Tomorrow we need to reaffirm that to be able to give you something more specific information.

‘There is no need of surgery which was the main fear because it would have ruled him out for months, so let’s see.’.

Pressed on whether Raya would be back in time to face Manchester City inSunday’s box office Premier League clash, Arteta said: ‘Again, tomorrow we will have more tests and then we will know.

Raya’s experienced compatriot, Kepa Arrizabalaga, replaced him as a substitute and St James’ Park and would likely start against Dortmund ahead of summer recruit Ilan Meslier, whose only Arsenal appearance so far came in the shock Carabao Cup fourth round defeat at Fleetwood Town last month.

‘We always assess every situation to make the right call,’ said Arteta when asked who will be selected to start in Raya’s absence.

‘It is quite clear what we are going to do.’.

According to recent reports, he added: ‘We know and we have seen what David brings to the team. That’s why we are well protected with Kepa and Illan.

‘That’s why everyone needs to be ready because these things unfortunately happen and now we need to show how well we are protected with the keepers we have in Kepa and Illan.’.

Steven Gerrard fears Mauricio Pochettino is already on collision course with one of his senior Manchester United players following Sunday’s damaging 4-0 defeat against Liverpool.

Any hope of a latest manager bounce was extinguished during a frantic opening quarter of an hour at Anfield yesterday when the hosts roared into a two goal lead following Leny Yoro’s sending off.

Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz piled on the agony in the closing stages and ensured the scoreline gave a more accurate representation of Liverpool’s near total dominance.

While playing the entire match at a numerical disadvantage certainly played a role in the one-sided nature of such an eagerly anticipated contest, United were second best from the off and were made to pay for their newly introduced manager’s questionable team selection.

The decision to drop Harry Maguire at the expense of Matthijs de Ligt, who is still feeling his way back from a long-term injury, was questioned by the likes of Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville before kick-off and their skepticism was vindicated when the Dutch centre-half played a role in Yoro’s red card.

Gerrard, meanwhile, went a step further in his criticism by accusing Pochettino of showing a lack of respect to Maguire by relegating him to the bench in his first game at the helm.

‘I thought he got it wrong,’ Gerrard told The Overlap. ‘I thought he got it wrong in the back line. I think to start someone in a game of that magnitude, it’s the biggest game in the country. All eyes are on it all over the world.

‘To play someone that hadn’t played since last November. You can understand the manager wanting to come in and put his stamp on it and change a few things that had been going on previously, but Harry Maguire’s their best defender at the moment.

It has been revealed that ‘Forget the youngsters that are maybe not ready at the moment. Matthijs de Ligt’s been out for a year. Harry Maguire’s their best defender at the moment. He should have started the game.

‘And he made a difference when he came on. And he was one who was putting his body on the line. He made a great block, I think it was around the 38th, 39th minute, which stopped a certain goal. And I’ve watched Manchester United a lot this season, and he’s one who’s having a go.

‘He’s one who is rolling his sleeves up and having a go. Okay, he hasn’t been perfect, but to not play him and put de Ligt in before him, I thought it was a bit disrespectful.’.

Pochettino and United will have to soldier on with what they have until January when the transfer window reopens and strengthening a defence which is now official the worst in Europe’s top five leagues will represent a priority.

Gerrard added: ‘It’s just who’s available and who wants to sell and let good players go at the moment, so they’re going to have to pay massive money.

‘There’s going to be a tax with that, because if United want to go and take, they need world-class centre-halves in January, cause waiting until the summer might be too late, so they need world-class centre-halves.

‘Who’s going to let world-class centre-halves go in January? Unless someone’s prepared to pay astronomical money. That’s what’s going to have to happen.’.

Luca Williams-Barnett revealed that Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi played a prank on the teenager ahead of his maiden Premier League goal for the club.

The 18-year-old grabbed the opener against Ipswich Town at the weekend, before going on to mark his first full Premier League start with an assist for Dominic Solanke.

The winger had been involved in the first-team squad for the last four Premier League games prior to the Ipswich match, and had continued to train with De Zerbi’s squad in the week.

As such, being told that he was playing for the Under-21s would have been a shock for the young star.

He revealed De Zerbi’s practical joke in an interview with SpursPlay: "The day before, the gaffer obviously pulled me aside.

"He actually said, ‘You’re going to be playing with the ‘21s, 60 minutes to get your legs back,’ and I was like, ‘What?’ but obviously he told me the news and the whole day I was just buzzing. I couldn’t wait.

"Everything I’ve dreamed of. Obviously scoring and getting an assist, it’s like a dream come true basically.".

Williams-Barnett admitted he thought he had spurned his chance for a dream debut, missing a similar opportunity to the move that led to his goal.

He said: “The first ball into the box I wasn’t really there and I was quite annoyed because it was open and I could have had the goal.

It has been revealed that “Once I saw it go back to Pedro [Porro], it was an instinct. Once I saw he was able to cross the ball, I just had to get behind my man and put the ball in the goal.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 10:10.

Stoke City square off against Millwall on Wednesday night looking for the win that would keep the club in the automatic promotion spots of the Championship table.

At a time when the Potters are in second position, Alex Neil visits one of his former club with the Lions beginning the week in 16th place.

The November international break came at the wrong time for Stoke, who have established themselves as contenders for promotion to the Premier League.

Nevertheless, Mark Robins's side returned on Saturday with a 1-0 win over then-leaders Birmingham City, making it 10 victories from their last 13 games in the Championship.

Rather incredibly, Stoke have accumulated 16 points from their last six games without scoring more than twice in a single match.

Just two goals have been conceded during that period, while Stoke have four clean sheets from their most recent six games at the bet365 Stadium, including their last three.

Despite starting the campaign with three successive defeats, no team in the Championship has won more games (10) than Stoke in 2026-27.

Meanwhile, Neil takes his players to one of his former employers with Millwall having lost five of their most recent seven games.

Three successive defeats, the latest being a 1-0 defeat to Queens Park Rangers, have essentially left the Scot fighting to keep his job at The Den.

Millwall, who reached the playoffs last season, are nine points adrift of eighth spot, and defeat to Stoke would leave the East London outfit cut adrift from the mid-table places.

As well as losing five of their eight away matches this campaign, Millwall have conceded 18 goals on their travels, the joint-second worst defensive record in such fixtures in the division.

Stoke could make at least three changes, a consequence of Luca Bombino's red card against Birmingham and Djibril Soumare and George Hirst both picking up injuries in the same game.

Eric-Junior Bocat should start at left wing-back, Svante Ingelsson is in line to feature in midfield should Ethan Galbraith not return after illness, and Sam Gallagher could get the nod ahead of Robert Bozenik in attack.

Million Manhoef may also start on one of the flanks should Robins wish to introduce further fresh legs.

Meanwhile, Alfie Doughty could be introduced as a straight replacement for suspended Millwall defender Zak Sturge.

When the Lions have failed to score in three successive matches, Zak Lovelace and Mihailo Ivanovic will also feel in contention to start in the final third.

Luke Cundle, Romain Esse and Josh Coburn will all be assessed after missing the QPR defeat on Saturday.

Stoke City possible starting lineup:.

Johansson; Wilmot, Lawal, Graham; Johnson, Ingelsson, McGlynn, Bocat; Devenny, Gallagher, Bae.

Millwall possible starting lineup:.

Jensen; Sykes, Taylor, Cooper, Doughty; De Norre, Metcalfe; Neghli, Arconte, Lovelace; Ivanovic.

While this contest could prove to be closer than many are anticipating, it is difficult to back against a Stoke side that are showing many battling qualities to stay in their current position. With that in mind, we are predicting a narrow win for the Potters.

Mikel Arteta has effectively confirmed that Kepa Arrizabalaga will start in goal for Arsenal in the absence of David Raya.

The Gunners will be without first-choice stopper Raya on Tuesday night for the Champions League match at home to Borussia Dortmund.

Arteta has split minutes in the Carabao Cup this season between back-up goalkeepers Kepa and Illan Meslier, but it is Kepa who has been on the bench throughout the Premier League season and he came on for Raya against Newcastle.

Discussing his options to replace Raya on Monday, Arteta indicated that Kepa is expected to serve as deputy.

“I think it’s clear for us who is going to play tomorrow,” the Arsenal boss remarked at his pre-Dortmund press conference.

Kepa started the Carabao Cup third round win over Ipswich earlier this season, but summer signing Meslier then got the nod in the shock last-16 defeat at fourth-tier Fleetwood.

It has been revealed that that was despite Kepa being fit and in the matchday squad. However, that was due to a desire to reward Meslier with an opportunity, rather than the Frenchman taking the No2 spot from Kepa.

“Because I want everybody to be part of it,” Arteta mentioned, explaining the decision to start Meslier against Fleetwood.

“To feel part of it, you need to play. Illan has been really good with us. We believed that it was the right thing to share those minutes in the competition.

Published: 18:17 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 18:22 EST, 21 November 2026.

Rangers manager Derek McInnes praised his side for having the mentality to grind out last-gasp winners and hailed their late victory over Motherwell as a ‘top-class performance’.

McInnes admits he would have liked a more comfortable evening from a match which saw his side fire 29 shots with 11 on target, but he was happy with the level of chance creation and delighted to see Ryan Naderi serve up yet another crucial goal with a deflected effort that made the difference two minutes from time.

Rangers had opened brightly with a Manny Fernandez goal on eight minutes, but looked like sliding to a third straight league draw away from home after Jake Girdwood-Reich had levelled for the home side in the first half.

‘I thought it was a very good, strong performance. I’ve just been told that every one of my outfield players had a shot,’ stated McInnes, whose men are four points behind Celtic with a game in hand against Aberdeen at Ibrox on Tuesday.

‘I’ve never known a team who practice so much shooting, and crossing and finishing during the week. It was the only thing missing for us, I thought it was a top class performance.

Industry observers note that ‘Away from home in the Premiership, you’re never going to dominate a whole game. There were little spells Motherwell had on transitions, but our press was strong and we were aggressive. I’m just disappointed it took so long to get the winning goal.

Derek McInnes revels in the victory at Motherwell at full-time.

Ryan naderi scored the dramatic late winner for Rangers as they closed the gap on Celtic.

Sources indicate that ‘Equally, on the sidelines, I felt a goal was coming. It’s OK me feeling that, but I think the players feel it too and it’s key they do. It would have been such a body blow if we hadn’t found a winning goal, given the stats and the performance.

‘It’s a tough away game and it’s the first time we’ve won here in three years, so that illustrates that.

‘When we pick the bones out of it, there will be a lot of what we ask for in that game.

According to recent reports, ‘It’s good that we’ve got that in us, a last minute goal, because we know how key they are in a campaign. I’ve never found mental strength an glitch for my side.

Industry observers note that ‘On this fantastic run, we’ve been very strong. We were by far the better team. We dominated the chances and a lot of what I was hoping for was there.

‘It was just that execution. We’ve had this story before, but, as long as we keep winning, I’m all right with that.

‘I’m getting asked about not putting teams to bed. That’s another away game with two goals. It’s four in a row now. In our last two home games, we’ve scored four and three, so scoring goals isn’t really causing a problem, even if people are looking for a negative.

‘I think that performance was an improvement from where we’ve been in recent weeks.’.

McInnes also reserved special praise for matchwinner Naderi.

Sources indicate that ‘Ryan’s game is really strong at the minute. He looks like a very confident boy and so he should be,’ stated the manager. ‘Wrongly now, when you think of Ryan or people ask me, it’s about him knocking his pan in.

‘His pressing is unbelievable and he’s a major horse up there. He runs and works and puts people under pressure, but he gets goals and has an influence. In that system tonight, his was the most vital position for us, in terms of running channels and getting hold of the ball.

Manny Fernandez opened the scoring for the Ibrox men in the 2-1 victory.

‘He led the line brilliantly. It was a proper No 9 performance.

Naderi admits he is delighted to be scoring messy goals that are making a real impact on his side’s challenge for the title.

In a recent development, ‘I like those games. Of course we would like to win 3-0, but, when you win in the last minute, that's something special,’ mentioned the Czech internationalist.

‘I can't score nice goals, only ugly ones.’.

Motherwell head coach Alfred Johansson remarked: ‘It is obviously tough to concede that goal at the very end. We had a feeling we could finish the game with a draw.

‘I think Rangers were better than us. They had a good start to the game and it was tough for us conceding a goal from a set-piece when we are not aggressive enough.

‘At the end, we lost the energy. Rangers were turning up the heat in the last 15, 20 minutes. We were fighting and surviving and then they scored.

‘Alex Paulsen played fantastic in goal. He has been making a lot of saves for us this season and, at the end, it is tough for him to concede a goal like that.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup will be hosted jointly by England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, FIFA have confirmed, with the tournament returning to the United Kingdom for the first time since 1966.

The UK was the sole bidder to host the tournament, and received a 4.3 out of 5 rating from FIFA evaluators.

Sources indicate that the bid has put forward 19 potential venues, including five in London: Wembley Stadium, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the Emirates, Stamford Bridge and a renovated Selhurst Park. Old Trafford will be considered, regardless of whether Manchester United moves to its proposed fresh home.

It has been revealed that some 32 teams will contest the 2027 World Cup in Brazil, but this is due to expand to 48 from 2031 onwards. The tournament, then, will comprise 104 matches.

According to recent reports, england has not hosted a major tournament since staging the women’s European Championships in 2022, which the Lionesses won. It has failed in bids to host the 2006 and 2018 men’s World Cups. England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland will jointly host the Men’s European Championship in 2028.

It is understood that the process of finalising the list of stadia that will be used is ongoing and is under FIFA’s jurisdiction. Wembley is the only stadium that currently meets the standards required to host the World Cup final.

Burnham calls for ambition after ‘deeply disappointing’ Cop31 disagreements.

South East Water slumps to loss after hefty bill from supply failures.

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean.

It is still to be decided how many of the co-host nations will qualify automatically for the tournament.

It has been revealed that the 2035 World Cup bid has also put forward a host stadium in Northern Ireland - Belfast’s Windsor Park - and two each in Scotland and Wales. The Scottish grounds are Glasgow’s Hampden Park and Edinburgh’s Easter Road, while the Welsh pair are both in Cardiff: the Millennium Stadium and the Cardiff City Stadium.

The remaining English host stadiums are: Villa Park, The AmEx, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, the City Ground, and the Stadium of Light.

Sources indicate that three more stadia could be added to the bid, most notably a potential latest Chelsea ground. Discussions as to the future of Stamford Bridge have been bubbling away for decades as the club’s hierarchy debate whether to redevelop the current ground, knock it down to build a new one on the current site, or move to a new site altogether.

Birmingham City’s new Powerhouse Stadium and Wrexham’s renovated Racecourse Ground could also host matches.

Recent findings suggest that prime Minister Andy Burnham welcomed the news, saying: “The world is coming to the United Kingdom. In 2035 the biggest tournament in women’s sport will be played in cities across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, bringing visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country.

“Our players have inspired a generation of girls. In 2035 that generation will watch the best in the world play on their doorstep - and some of them will be on the pitch. But the impact of this World Cup will go much further. It will reach into communities across the country, bring more people into the game and leave a legacy that lasts long after the final whistle.”.

In a recent development, FA CEO Mark Bullingham said: “Hosting Euro 2022 allowed us to change the game in our country, by creating a generation of aspirational role models and growing demand from women and girls to play. Hosting a World Cup would give us the chance to build on that across all four nations.”.

England last hosted a World Cup in 1966, when the men’s team famously beat West Germany 4-2 in the final to seal the nation’s first major honour. The Lionesses have since become back-to-back Euros champions in 2022 and 2025, but suffered World Cup final heartbreak in 2023 when they were beaten 1-0 by Spain in Sydney.

Before the UK’s host bid for 2035 was confirmed at a special FIFA Congress, it was also revealed that a joint bid by the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica had been approved to host the 2031 World Cup.

Corriere dello Sport handed Esposito an overall performance rating of 8/10 and branded the striker "unstoppable" for his excellent display.

Meanwhile, Sky Sport Italia gave him Inter's highest rating of 8/10.

Esposito has scored 10 times in 15 appearances for Italy, and he seemingly has the skill set to be a huge success in the Premier League.

Thibaut Courtois described Jude Bellingham as a "leader" on the pitch for Real Madrid, saying Los Blancos' chances of silverware this season may rest with the midfielder.

Courtois' comments came ahead of Madrid's Champions League clash with PSV on Tuesday, with Jose Mourinho's side winning all four of their games in Europe so far.

Madrid are on a nine-game winning run across all competitions, the latest of which came in dramatic fashion against Celta Vigo at the weekend, with Carlos Espi coming off the bench to save his team once again with an 85th-minute winner.

Recent findings suggest that bellingham was also on target in what was his 100th LaLiga appearance. He has now scored three goals in his last four games, having failed to net in his previous seven.

Since joining from Borussia Dortmund in 2023, Bellingham has played 182 times for Madrid in all competitions, scoring 60 goals as well as providing 41 assists.

He has six goals and three assists so far in 2026-27, and Courtois believes Bellingham is one of Madrid's most important players despite only being 23 years of age.

"Jude is a young guy but when you see him, it feels like he's a few years older," Courtois told reporters when asked about Bellingham's most impressive qualities.

"In the beginning, when you compare him with Arda [Guler], Arda was a quieter kid. With Jude, you already feel like he had a presence, but there isn't much difference in age.

In a recent development, "Jude is someone who really wants to win. That's why on the field he swears a lot! He's really a winner, and when he's not happy, he will make it known.

"He's also a leader on the field. He's a great player, a great mentality. You need those kinds of people like that in your team that go for everything.

Sources indicate that "It seems like he has an engine to play 200 minutes. He keeps on going, running with the ball, it's really hard to dispossess him.

"And on the outside, he just works hard, he goes to the gym. With a good Jude, we play better.".

The Red Devils were down to ten men inside eight minutes when Leny Yoro was sent off for denying Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Shares in the artificial intelligence firm Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Thursday, in the biggest initial public offering of all time.Credit: Idrees Mohammed/AFP via Getty.
  • In a recent development, anthropic, the frontier artificial-intelligence company, has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November.
  • Recent findings suggest that the maker of AI model Claude, Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a group who broke away from rival giant OpenAI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shares in the artificial intelligence firm Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Thursday, in the biggest initial public offering of all time.Credit: Idrees Mohammed/AFP via Getty.

In a recent development, anthropic, the frontier artificial-intelligence company, has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November. With a staggering valuation of around US$1.5 trillion, the firm, based in San Francisco, California, is now among the world’s most valuable companies — and it has major ambitions in science.

Recent findings suggest that the maker of AI model Claude, Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a group who broke away from rival giant OpenAI. Its models have proven powerful in research, and Anthropic has launched its own directed science effort, focusing on areas including quantum mechanics and protein design. This year alone, it has reported mathematics breakthroughs and launched its first life sciences laboratory.

According to recent reports, the IPO might also unleash a historic wave of philanthropy: all seven of Anthropic’s founders are likely to become billionaires and have pledged to donate 80% of their equity in the company to charity, including chief executive Dario Amodei. And on 18 October, the company announced that it had established the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, created to support initiatives that benefit society and stocked with an initial commitment of 5% of Anthropic’s shares.

But the firm has drawn criticism from researchers, who say its aims of curing diseases on short timescales are unrealistic and that its race towards developing ultra-powerful, ‘superintelligent’ AI models pose serious risks, including an existential threat to humanity. In its public prospectus, published ahead of the IPO, Anthropic outlines a new governance structure that it says is “consistent with our commitment to AI safety and responsibility”, and adds that safety research directly shapes the firm’s “model design, training, and deployment.”.

Nature looks at four areas of science where Anthropic is making waves.

AI’s potential to turbocharge the discovery of fresh medicines has been a centerpiece of Anthropic’s pitch to investors. “If today we look at things like cancer, Alzheimer’s, heart disease, mental illness — these will be relics of the past in, I think, less than a decade,” Amodei said in a promotional video ahead of the IPO.

It has been revealed that the company has been rapidly expanding its biomedical ambitions. This year, Anthropic opened its first ‘wet’ laboratory for life sciences research, declared partnerships with several pharmaceutical companies, and remarked it was pursuing drug leads of its own. “We plan to scale this work up substantially from here,” the company said on 27 October.

Anthropic bought a one-person, AI-powered biotech: is this drug discovery’s future?

Anthropic bought a one-person, AI-powered biotech: is this drug discovery’s future?

But Amodei’s habit of promising swift, AI-fueled cures for complex diseases has rankled many researchers and entrepreneurs in the field who feel the timeline is unrealistic.

Industry observers note that over the last year, Anthropic has made a major push in the life sciences. In June, the organization hired John Jumper, who shared the 2024 Chemistry Nobel Prize for his work on AlphaFold2 while at Google DeepMind in London.

Some of the tech giant’s early biological research received a mixed reception from biologists. After Anthropic reported using a swarm of AI agents to find signs of a new CRISPR-like system in viral sequence data, some researchers questioned the novelty of the finding and noted that the company had not carried out the experimental work needed to determine the system’s function.

It has been revealed that in protein design — a field that has boomed thanks to specialist AI tools including AlphaFold — Anthropic’s work has also failed to generate much excitement. In August, Anthropic used Claude Science — an agentic system that can access other biological tools and databases — to make novel ‘binders’ against 15 protein targets.

It has been revealed that “Expectations are sky high,” notes Anthony Gitter, a computational biologist at the Morgridge Institute for Research in Madison, Wisconsin. “I understand why some view their initial public results as underwhelming.”.

Sources indicate that but Gitter is enthusiastic about Anthropic’s protein design efforts, largely because the manufacturer was transparent about the work, from the prompts it used to the sequences that were generated. “I would strongly encourage Anthropic to continue that in their future life sciences research,” Gitter adds.

In recent months, Anthropic and other companies — notably Google DeepMind and OpenAI — have been working to establish their research credentials in large part by showing off the rapidly growing mathematical abilities of their flagship AI models.

In a recent development, on 7 September Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge and collaborator Tristan Buckmaster at Latest York University solved a special case of the Navier-Stokes equations, a long-standing problem in mathematical physics that describes the flow of fluids. Hours after Anthropic revealed the result, OpenAI claimed a full solution of the problem, igniting a controversy.

In a recent development, in another collaboration, Alpöge and mathematical physicist Ethan Sussman at Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois, have been working towards establishing the mathematical foundations of the standard model of particle physics. This too is a problem on which OpenAI has made similar claims.

Anthropic and its competitors see the ability to write a rigorous proof of a mathematical fact as a crucial testing ground for their reasoning models. That’s in large part because the correctness of a proof is an objective measure that can be used as a ‘reward’ to further train AI systems.

There will be some games where Mikel Arteta has no choice but to tweak the XI, rest some tired legs and give his second-choice attackers the chance – although given the option he may wish to pick the same team every week.

The three substantial guns of his attack were primed and ready to come on in the next break in play when Arsenal at last broke through in this, their second Champions League league phase game of the season against some stubborn opposition from Ligue 1. Lille had sat deep against an Arsenal attack without Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, and the French club were past the hour when it all finally broke.

It has been revealed that that was a superb finish from Jurrien Timber who, with two touches, demonstrated that in the modern era even defenders are capable of the kind of moments of skill and composure that we once assumed were only within the capacity of the best attackers. He gave Arsenal the lead just as Mikel Arteta had decided he had seen enough from some of his second-choice attackers – Viktor Gyokeres, Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino. They had created some chances and at times looked promising, but as soon as the big three were on the difference was obvious.

It has been revealed that “It was a joy to watch,” Arteta stated. “The three goals were unbelievable, the connections, the timings, the quality they delivered to score. Even Arteta, no sentimentalist, insisted on beginning his press conference with a tribute.

For Arteta’s players, there will be a much bigger test than this one in Munich next week against Bayern. Arsenal have already won in Naples but a victory at Bayern would be significant beyond that. The moment we started to do that better, we could counter-press, and start to play into the opposition’s box, and with the quality that we have we made a real difference there.

I had some moments in the first half but second half I had more. First touch was good, which was half the job, and then Noni [Madueke] was screaming “shoot” so I thought OK I have to shoot. And then yeah it went in nice.

I wasn’t thinking too much. I saw the goal and thought I need to shoot. We needed that first goal, we were playing well just needed the goal. Happy to get that for the team.

Michael Olise was sent off in Bayern Munich’s draw at Viking, meaning he will miss next week’s game against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena.

Since returning to the competition under Arteta in 2023, they have won all 12 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals.

Including knock-out games, Arsenal have conceded just eight goals in 20 home matches, keeping 15 clean sheets.

Two wins from two in the Champions League for Arsenal, joining Sporting and Barcelona as the teams with a 100 per cent record.

Arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

Sources indicate that as Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”.

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

Sources indicate that lille sell their best players every summer. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

Leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. After leaving the Emirates, Giroud went on to score against Arsenal for Chelsea in the 2019 Europa League final, but he can still expect a warm reception.

Arsenal’s home record in the Champions League has been formidable since they returned to the competition under Arteta in 2023. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool have lost a number of their key players on free transfers over the last three years.

Trent Alexander-Arnold, Ibrahima Konate, Mohamed Salah and Roberto Firmino are just some of the players to have left Anfield at the end of their contracts in recent seasons.

The club have become accustomed to letting some of their best players run their contracts down, and it has cost them in the past.

Now, several of Andoni Iraola's key players are entering the final six months of their contracts, and negotiations can soon begin with potential suitors.

One of Liverpool's out-of-contract stars is attracting plenty of interest, and the Reds really could lose him for nothing.

Virgil van Dijk has been absolutely key to Iraola's defence so far this season and is still one of the best performing defenders in the Premier League.

The Dutchman will soon enter the final six months of his deal however, and will then be free to negotiate with clubs from abroad over a free transfer in the summer.

Juventus and AC Milan are the two clubs reported leading the way for the colossus, with the pair keeping a close eye on his contract situation.

That's according to an revision from Ekrem Konur, who claims that Italy's two most decorated clubs are ready to battle for Van Dijk's signature.

Conversations over an extension at Anfield are reportedly ongoing, but are yet to bare any fruit, and the future of the Dutchman still remains very uncertain.

Liverpool's recruitment plans seem to hinge heavily on whether or not the skipper puts pen to paper on a new deal, but the partnership formed between Jeremy Jacquet and Van Dijk is something that the Reds won't want to lose.

It isn't yet clear where Van Dijk's preferences lie if a upcoming deal cannot be agreed, but as January edges closer it feels more and more likely that the defender could be playing his final season in Merseyside.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Cole Palmer was involved in a frustrated exchange with team-mate Joao Pedro after Chelsea crashed to a 4-1 home defeat against Leeds.
  • The Blues were beaten by Leeds at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 1999, despite having taken the lead through Emmanuel Emegha's first goal for the club.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 16:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 21 November 2026.

Cole Palmer was involved in a frustrated exchange with team-mate Joao Pedro after Chelsea crashed to a 4-1 home defeat against Leeds.

The Blues were beaten by Leeds at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 1999, despite having taken the lead through Emmanuel Emegha's first goal for the club.

Noah Okafor scored twice for Leeds either side of a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty, with Brenden Aaronson adding a fourth in stoppage time.

Palmer, who opted against going around the pitch applauding the remaining fans at full-time, was captured approaching Joao Pedro following the match.

The Chelsea star could be seen covering his mouth while speaking to his team-mate, who had been left to watch from the sidelines as he continues his recovery from injury.

Joao Pedro put his hand on Palmer's shoulder as he responded to his team-mate, with the Brazilian then shrugging his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer went to walk down the tunnel.

Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels.

Joao Pedro shrugged his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer headed down the tunnel after their exchange. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels.

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso was asked post-match about the exchange, amid a suggestion Joao Pedro and Willie Isa, Chelsea's player support and development officer, had attempted to persuade Palmer to applaud the fans.

‘No, we were disappointed, the fans were disappointed because the expectations from them are high,' Alonso responded.

'We feel sorry for them and we need to go through together and to find solutions to that and now, as I stated, for sure it’s not the easiest moment.

‘It’s a fragile moment but we need to work together and stick together because there is still such a long way to go.'.

Alonso's side have now lost three of their last four Premier League matches, having been beaten at home by rivals Tottenham and falling to defeat at Sunderland prior to the international break.

The Blues have now dropped to eighth in the table, with Alonso's side having won five, drawn one and lost five of their 11 matches to date.

Palmer had begun the season brightly under Alonso by scoring in their opening two fixtures but has only scored one league goal since, netting with a penalty in a 2-0 win over Man United.

Chelsea will look to bounce back when they face struggling Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two matches, before blockbuster clashes with Liverpool and Man City.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 12:02.

Sources indicate that paris Saint-Germain have recently made enquiries about Estevao and Rayan, who are not available in the January transfer window. The capital club have a third, more accessible Brazilian talent on their radar.

Sources indicate that injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue could force PSG to revise their intends for the January window. Both forwards have suffered anterior cruciate ligament ruptures and could miss the whole season. Faced with these two major absences, boss Luis Enrique and Luis Campos are studying different options to strengthen the Parisian attack.

With Eli Junior Kroupi and Paris Brunner ruled out as options, the French club have notably made enquiries about three young Brazilian talents in recent weeks, according to TeamTalk.

PSG contacted Chelsea to find out the conditions of a possible transfer for Estevao. The 19-year-old winger, who arrived from Palmeiras, is highly rated by the Parisian hierarchy. His limited playing time this season had raised hopes of an opening, but Chelsea quickly ruled out that possibility.

The London club are counting on their Brazil international for the coming years and do not wish to part with him, even temporarily.

Industry observers note that the situation is similar for Rayan. The 20-year-old winger, who plays for Bournemouth, is also on the Parisian radar. But Bournemouth are no more inclined to let their gem leave in the middle of the season.

According to the outlet, another Brazilian gem is being closely watched by the Parisian recruiters: Alisson Santana.

The 21-year-old winger at the moment plays for Shakhtar Donetsk and is enjoying a convincing start to the season. The Brazilian has scored six goals and provided five assists in 16 games. His performances have attracted the attention of PSG scouts.

Over the last couple of years, Liverpool have had a lot of work that they've needed to do on their squad.

Well over £600 million has been spent on newly introduced players by them so far and, right now, it's still unclear whether they're actually any better off than they were when Jurgen Klopp was in charge.

Obviously, some arrivals such as Ronald Araujo have been a major upgrade on Jeremie Frimpong but, for others such as Bradley Barcola, some questions still remain.

However, with a lot of Liverpool's focus during the last summer window going on their attack and defence, it feels like the club should now be spending most of their time trying to improve their midfield.

Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai may have been handed new long-term deals last season but, thanks to the way Andoni Iraola uses his midfielders, neither of them have really met expectations.

So, it will hardly come as a surprise to see fresh midfielders already being linked with Liverpool.

Liverpool could make a surprise move for Leeds United midfielder Ao Tanaka.

Right now, one of Liverpool's biggest problem areas is their midfield.

As mentioned, a couple of Iraola's current options just aren't cut out for the double pivot role that he wants his midfielders to play.

However, since they didn't sign any latest central midfielders in the summer, it feels like that could be their next port of call in January.

Many major-name players have been linked with an Anfield switch but, a surprise option has just emerged.

Ao Tanaka is currently plying his trade for Leeds United.

And, even though he was signed by them back when they were in the Championship, he's quickly managed to adjust to life as a Premier League player.

This season alone, the number six has featured in 12 games across all competitions for the West Yorkshire outfit and, according to TEAMtalk, thanks to the fact that his contract expires in 2028, Liverpool have thrown their hat into the ring.

The Japanese international is 28 years old with this deal feeling eerily similar to the one that Klopp struck with VfB Stuttgart for Wataru Endo a few years ago.

Tanaka has plenty of Premier League experience under his belt and, for the right price, he could be a solid signing for Liverpool.

Ao Tanaka would be a very out there signing for Liverpool.

A upcoming number six should be high on Liverpool's priority list.

Without a new one being brought in, the Reds are going to fall even further behind their title rivals than they presently are.

Indeed, other areas of their squad also need upgrading but, without a new defensive midfielder being brought in, they're always going to be on the backfoot.

Because, even though Alexis Mac Allister and Trey Nyoni are both playing well in their defensive midfield roles, if one of them ends up injured, the Reds are done.

Iraola knows this and by now, you'd hope that Julian Ward does too.

Of course, January is a notoriously hard time to strike deals for players with their prices often being inflated but, in the grand scheme of things, signing someone such as Tanaka, even just as a back-up makes an awful lot of sense.

He'd probably be available for a cut-rate deal and, since he's now 28 years old, this could be his last chance to make a substantial move.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 12:25.
  • Chelsea's 4-1 defeat at home to Leeds United has strengthened the opinion that Xabi Alonso may not necessarily be the correct fit as Chelsea manager.
  • Not only has the Spaniard defended the multiple occasions that Chelsea have allowed opponents to have the majority of possession, he was seemingly dismissive to the suggestion from the media that his players lack the physicality to compete against the majority of the teams in the Premier League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 12:25.

Chelsea's 4-1 defeat at home to Leeds United has strengthened the opinion that Xabi Alonso may not necessarily be the correct fit as Chelsea manager.

Not only has the Spaniard defended the multiple occasions that Chelsea have allowed opponents to have the majority of possession, he was seemingly dismissive to the suggestion from the media that his players lack the physicality to compete against the majority of the teams in the Premier League.

Should Chelsea lose at Nottingham Forest - another team far more physically-imposing than themselves - on Friday night, Alonso's win percentage after 15 matches would be almost identical to that of Liam Rosenior's after 23 games.

While that creates an argument that Chelsea's players are to blame for their fall from grace rather than the Spaniard or Englishman, Alonso is responsible for a number of baffling decisions during his time at Stamford Bridge.

Here, Sports Mole highlights nine mistakes that Alonso has made since he was revealed as the club's latest manager in May.

With Valentin Barco announcing that he was leaving Strasbourg on May 19, the deal to take him to fellow BlueCo-owned club Chelsea could have been concluded before Alonso's appointment.

However, for unknown reasons, it was not announced until August 2, suggesting that there was time for Alonso to veto the transfer.

In a recent development, at 5ft 7ins and of slender build, Barco is simply not equipped to be a Premier League midfielder. While he may have starred for Strasbourg, the Argentine is not a suitable fit alongside Chelsea's other engine-room options.

He has reached this stage of the season with three starts and four substitute appearances, with just 25 minutes coming since October 10.

Given the amount of game time that Marco Palestra was given during pre-season, it was clear that Alonso viewed the Italian as a first-choice pick at full-back or wing-back.

In a recent development, nevertheless, Alonso got carried away. Palestra racked up 311 minutes across four pre-season friendlies played between August 1 and August 15, and the former Atalanta BC player suffered an injury in the days before the opening Premier League game of the season against Fulham.

That prevented the Serie A defender of the year from making his debut until October 10, effectively having to play catch-up as he attempts to acclimatise to English football.

While the 21-year-old started the recent win over Manchester United, he is yet to convince in his current role.

After an extended season that saw him represent Ecuador at the World Cup on July 1, Moises Caicedo was back playing friendlies for Chelsea in the Middle East by August 5.

The midfielder subsequently started three friendlies across 10 days and, like Palestra, suffered an injury in the build-up to the Fulham game.

Caicedo then lasted just 14 minutes on his return from the substitutes' bench against Brighton & Hove Albion six days later and was not seen again until October 10.

He has suffered with a lingering issue ever since, and the way in which Alonso used players during pre-season deserves more scrutiny than it has done.

Alonso went from naming a stronger team than anticipated against Luton Town in the EFL Cup second round to making many alterations versus Leeds United in round three.

Some of that decision-making was justified, yet Alonso himself has taken responsibility for making what he notes were too many changes for the latter match.

Chelsea ultimately came from 2-0 down to prevail by a 6-3 scoreline in a crazy game, but withdrawing Estevao Willian after 45 minutes started the ball rolling when it came to the Brazilian's frustration over his game time.

Not only did Jordan Henderson make his first start since the World Cup, with no pre-season, in this match, Alonso partnered the veteran Englishman with Barco, who was making his first Premier League start for Chelsea.

Although Chelsea held Brentford for the first hour and Henderson produced a solid performance on debut, this game exposed that Barco weakens Chelsea's midfield, rather than add any match-winning qualities.

Romeo Lavia also remained an unused substitute in this contest, one which Chelsea lost by a 3-0 scoreline.

While some Chelsea fans had been waiting for Geovany Quenda to be handed his first start for Chelsea, they did not anticipate it coming in a London derby against Tottenham Hotspur.

Furthermore, his selection led to Morgan Rogers taking on the number nine role, rather than Danny Welbeck, in the absence of the injured Joao Pedro.

It has been revealed that chelsea subsequently produced one of their most ineffective performances in the final third this season. That was not necessarily because of Quenda, but more through a lack of a traditional number nine to trouble the Spurs defence.

Two weeks later, Alonso chose the same approach against Sunderland, this time using Pedro Neto down the middle.

This decision was essentially made because Chelsea beat Manchester United in the previous game, yet the Red Devils had been the better team in the first half at Stamford Bridge without scoring their opener.

Although there is an argument that Welbeck has not made the expected impact at Chelsea, the 35-year-old has not been given a chance to build up any rhythm and is immediately benched on the back of an ineffective performance.

Despite Emiliano Martinez being signed from Aston Villa to be Chelsea's number one, the Argentine had hardly been at his best prior to suffering a fractured jaw at Everton on October 17.

Meanwhile, Mike Penders recovered from a mistake on his first Premier League start against Spurs to deliver strong showings versus Liverpool, Manchester United and Sunderland, with the only two goals that he conceded coming from penalties.

Regardless, Martinez was back in the starting lineup against Leeds on Saturday, the 34-year-old conceding four goals and making Chelsea appear more vulnerable in defence than they already were.

Alonso has previously indicated that players will be selected on form, but this was a glaring example of choosing status over performances.

Martinez has now conceded 15 goals in 615 minutes for Chelsea. Penders has shipped seven goals in 555 minutes.

Estevao had already struggled against Leeds earlier this season, so the starlet being drafted back into the Chelsea XI for a second Stamford Bridge game versus the Yorkshire giants felt strange.

Furthermore, his inclusion was ahead of Neto, who is Chelsea's strongest winger when it comes to strength and defending. Alonso has already recognised this by using the Portuguese as a wing-back this season.

Neto being omitted from the first XI for a game against opponents of the profile of Leeds made no sense and was more muddled thinking from Alonso. Chelsea were already 3-1 down before he was introduced as a substitute.

Chelsea striker Emmanuel Emegha has revealed that he was “robbed” following Saturday’s Premier League match against Leeds.

Industry observers note that sources close to the Dutchman say that while his phone was not among the possessions stolen, personal belongings and several work-related items were taken. The incident took place outside a hotel in Mayfair on Saturday night.

Emegha was unhurt, with Chelsea understood to be aware of the situation and providing their full support to the player.

Emegha scored against Leeds on what was his first Premier League start for Chelsea since arriving from BlueCo sister club Strasbourg in the summer, but his goal made little difference in the end as Leeds won 4-1 against Xabi Alonso’s side.

“Unfortunately after the game I was robbed,” Emegha wrote. “I am okay and thankfully no one was hurt. Thanks for the messages of support.”.

The post started: “First goal, disappointing result, we’ll be back stronger on Friday [against Nottingham Forest].”.

Emegha’s transfer to Chelsea was agreed in September 2025 but he remained at Strasbourg last season and arrived at Stamford Bridge in the summer.

He scored 31 goals in 78 total appearances for Strasbourg across all competitions and opened his account for Chelsea on his third outing.

After nursing a hamstring injury at the beginning of the season, he made his first competitive appearance off the bench in Chelsea’s Carabao Cup last-16 defeat by Liverpool last month before then being handed a league debut in the 1-0 loss at Sunderland before the international break.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 12:42.

Enzo Maresca has provided a positive injury update on Manchester City’s Matheus Nunes ahead of Tuesday’s Champions League clash with Napoli at the Etihad Stadium.

The 28-year-old was unable to recover in time from an ankle problem to feature in City’s 1-1 Premier League draw with Fulham on Saturday.

Nunes has been absent for four of the Citizens’ last seven games in all tournaments this term, but Maresca confirmed at a pre-match press conference on Monday that the right-back “is back” and ready to face Napoli.

"Matheus is back. Then the only one [out] is still Antoine [Semenyo],” Maresca told reporters. “The rest, we have some doubts in terms of tiredness, amount of games, and we have today's session and then we'll decide.".

Sources indicate that pushed for more details on Nunes’s recent injury, Maresca added: "This one has been a little bit his ankle, but now he's fine. It's also normal with the amount of games we have, that's why also sometimes I try to rotate players.

"I've said many times, we need to not think about a sprint, we need to think about a marathon; 65 games. So I would like to use the strongest one every game, but then we destroy them. It's also a matter of trying to manage them the best way.”.

Nunes has established himself as Man City’s first-choice right-back when fit and available, while Abdukodir Khusanov and Rico Lewis have also been used on the right side of defence under Maresca and predecessor Pep Guardiola.

Man City’s No.27 has played 10 times across all competitions so far this season, but he has been left out of the matchday squad for five games due to injury or fitness-related issues.

In a recent development, "Since we started, we've used Rico [Lewis at right-back], but also [Khusanov], who I think he can play there,” Maresca explained. “For sure, it's much better... I'm trying to find the right balance.

Sources indicate that "If you ask me if Khusa is a better right-back or central defender, no doubt: Central defender. I know that. But it's a matter of the game, the players we have available.

"But Matheus [Nunes] has done very good since we started, the games he has played, overall he was very good. Rico has [also] done very good so far.”.

It remains to be seen whether Maresca will throw Nunes straight back into the starting lineup against Napoli, with one eye possibly on Sunday’s crucial Premier League showdown with Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium.

Man City have won three of their first four Champions League games in the League Phase and can strengthen their automatic last-16 qualification hopes with a victory against Napoli, who have lost three of their opening four matches in the competition.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ruben Amorim insisted that he and his AC Milan team are not getting carried away despite hammering Frosinone, and are simply focusing on the next game.

Milan were in a rampant mood tonight at San Siro, as they put five goals past Massimiliano Alvini’s side and it could have been more in truth. Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all scored, in addition to an own-goal that opened the scoring.

Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It was important that the Rossoneri build on their victory over Genoa before the break, especially given that Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus all won earlier in the round. In addition to that, several individuals shone and the team showed the levels that they are capable of.

Industry observers note that now, the challenge is to follow it up and get back on course in the Europa League in Greece on Thursday night. Amorim spoke to Sky after the final whistle to reflect on what was a very positive night for his side, with his words relayed by MilanNews.

Is that the best Milan performance since you have been here?

“It’s a good feeling, but it’s not just the result: it’s also about consistency throughout the 90 minutes of the match, but now we’re thinking about the next one. It’s always like that at this club, always thinking about the next one.

“Tonight we played well, we were intelligent, courageous, and it indicated towards the end of the match. We were tired, yet Frosinone continued to make transitions, but we managed to control them well.

In a recent development, “We could have even scored more goals. Perhaps in the middle of the first half we struggled a little and we need to improve in one-on-one situations defensively, but anyway, it was a good night for us tonight.”.

Sources indicate that are you happy for Gonçalo Ramos? How is he?

In a recent development, “We can’t lose any more players. All our players can play every game, but we have little time to recover for the Europa League, so we can’t risk anything. It was better to take him off.

“I imagine he wasn’t happy, but I’m still happy for him, for his goal, especially for the 2-0. It was a goal that made the difference in a match against a team that is very strong in one-on-one transitions.”.

Is Rabiot one of the best you’ve ever coached?

It has been revealed that “I don’t want to say he could have had a better career because he played at PSG. Now he’s here at Milan and we want him to stay.

“Obviously, he’s a player who can play as a number 10, as an attacking midfielder, he can also play as a number 8, he can also play as a slightly deeper playmaker, even if he doesn’t like it.

“He’s definitely one of the best players I’ve ever coached, he’s one of the best midfielders in Europe right now.”.

What will you say ahead of Olympiacos?

“The first thing I’ll say is that we have to win the match: if we don’t, then it will be really difficult to qualify for the next stage. Then I think that with Rabiot and Pulisic’s characteristics of playing between the lines, when they can’t play, we have to play and approach the game differently.

It has been revealed that “But that’s not an excuse. I mentioned the same things against Ferencváros: we should have played a different game and gotten a different result, but what I’m trying to say is that if we don’t win the match, it will be really difficult and things will go badly for us.

It has been revealed that “Then, if we exit the Europa League, we’ll only play once a week and many players won’t play enough. However, I think that if we stay in Europe, we can play more and everyone will continue to grow.

Industry observers note that “Furthermore, if we don’t qualify, we will fail to achieve an notable objective: so that’s why we have to start the match differently than Benfica and Ferencváros. We’ll see.”.

What can you tell us about Cisse as a striker?

Sources indicate that “I think he can play very well in that role, in that position. Tonight I chose Cissé to play in that position and not Camarda because against Frosinone, one-on-one, Cissé has these characteristics more. Tonight the goal wasn’t to keep possession, but to run and attack the space.

“Cissé is better at this than Camarda. We wanted to make more transitions than Frosinone, so it was a choice dictated by the player’s characteristics, but I think Cissé is good both as an attacking midfielder and as a central striker, and not just as a winger.”.
